data.description:
Night falls heavy.



The air tastes like copper and ozone.



Every lantern in Seichi has gone dark — all but one.



At the center of Freedom State, the Lantern of Balance burns like an emerald star, its light bending the air itself.



The laughter is gone. What remains is worse: silence so thick it feels alive.



The green fire shifts, drawing itself upward into a familiar shape — tall, thin, and smiling beneath a half-cracked mask.



Grimjack: “You chased echoes and called it courage.

But courage without memory is just another kind of fear.”


The cobblestones split beneath your feet, glowing with thin veins of green fire. Momo steps forward beside you, trembling but unbroken.



The lantern flares once, and the world turns blinding.
data.successDescription:
By dusk, Freedom State will be whole again.
 But when next year’s lanterns rise, every villager will glance twice at the color of the flame — just to make sure it stays gold.

data.name: Blacksteel Tides
data.description: The Order launders its blacksteel through the free port at Wake Island. Enter the island's sparring circuit as cover, follow the tide manifests, and earn the case officer's exam recommendation.
data.successDescription: Circuit fought, shipment stopped, Chunin Exams recommendation signed.

objectives.description: Sealed orders reach you a week after your debrief. The officer's hand: the Order launders blacksteel through the free port at Wake Island, where no village law reaches. Go there. Enter the island's sparring circuit as your cover, and keep your eyes on the water.
Travel to Wake Island, the neutral ground beyond village law.
The circuit master looks you over in a converted fish hall that smells of salt and old blood. Village stamps mean nothing here, they say. The circuit ranks you by wins. Everyone talks to a winner.
Win spars to establish yourself in the Wake Island circuit.

Three wins buys you a bench and a bowl. The fighters talk freely now: crates with violet seams move through the night docks, and the crews that carry them never drink at the circuit. Somebody pays them too well to be seen.
Climb the circuit rankings. The finalists know the island best.

A finalist with burn-scarred hands pulls you aside after your bout. I carried those crates once, they say, flexing fingers that no longer fully close. The manifests go through the harbor office. What is on them is not on any tide chart.
Make your way to the harbor office on the far side of Wake Island.
Recover a discarded tide manifest scrap from the sea-lane caches.
The scrap decodes against the officer's cipher from your Trials days. A shipment moves tonight, two handlers, out along the shallows. Blacksteel does not swim. Stop it before it sinks out of reach.
Intercept the shipment and defeat the two handlers before the cargo disappears.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description: The handlers slipped you in the shallows. Return to the circuit, patch up, and read the tides again.

The cargo sits beached and violet-veined at your feet. Word travels fast on a small island: by morning, the circuit knows exactly what you are, and nobody minds. Wake Island respects a winner with a cause.

The officer arrives on the next tide, in person, and reads everything twice in a rented back room. Then they produce a form you have never seen and sign it without ceremony. My recommendation for the Chunin Exams, they say. When you pass, there is a stronghold at your level waiting. The Order keeps a CHUNIN operation too.
Circuit champion, evidence secured, recommendation signed. Wake Island will remember you. So will the Order.

data.description:
As autumn settles over Seichi, Freedom State comes alive with color and sound. Paper lanterns hang from every eave, their golden light spilling across the stone paths. Masks of foxes and spirits dangle from vendor stalls, laughter drifts between the scent of chestnuts and incense, and for once, the world feels safe enough to celebrate.



This is Veilnight — a festival born from remembrance and rebirth.



Once a solemn rite to honor the dead, it has become a gathering of unity — a time to remember what survived, and who did not. Masks keep the spirits from wandering too close; lanterns light their way home.



Visitors from every village arrive by the hundreds, crowding Freedom State’s bridges and narrow streets. Musicians tune their shamisen, children chase each other through hanging gourds, and the central plaza glows beneath the towering Lantern of Balance — a great bronze beacon whose flame burns steady and gold.



Tonight marks a year since Seichi rebuilt.



Tonight, the veil thins.



And for the first time in a long time, no one is afraid.
data.successDescription:
When you finally find her beneath the hanging bridge, her eyes soften — but the lanterns above remain green, unchanging and unnatural.

The warmth of the festival has vanished.

And somewhere in the distance, the laughter begins again.

objectives.description: The festival is in full bloom. Music echoes from every corner of the plaza, merchants trade charms for coin and laughter, and the night hums with a warmth that feels almost fragile. At the foot of the Lantern of Balance, Dusk steps forward to address the gathered crowd. His voice cuts through the noise, calm and sure.
“Tonight we gather not to mourn, but to remember. The veil may thin—but Seichi still stands bright beneath it.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Stop paying attention and look around

objectives.description: Applause rolls through the square. The lanterns sway gently overhead, their flames steady and gold. Then the wind dies.  A faint vibration ripples through the plaza — soft, rhythmic, almost like laughter.  Every lantern flickers once… and turns green.
“You dressed your fear in paper and flame, and called it a festival.  Let’s see what happens when the lanterns start to burn.”
The change is silent and instant. The warm glow of the festival transforms into a sickly emerald light that paints every mask, every face, every wall.

The voice doesn’t come from anywhere — it’s simply there, inside the sound of the air itself. The green light deepens, shadows lengthen, and something shifts in the crowd. A single Momo shrieks. Its eyes flash green and its cheerful expression twists into a grin far too wide. Another follows. Then another. The laughter spreads.

nextObjectiveId.text: Become alert and reach for your kunai
Laugh awkwardly and try to blend in

objectives.description: Before you can react, your own Momo forces itself into being in a burst of emerald light.  The warmth that once surrounded her is gone; her giggle is wrong — higher, sharper.  She twirls midair, snickers, and darts into the winding festival streets.

nextObjectiveId.text: Try and grab your Momo before she can escape

objectives.description: The square erupts into panic. Villagers scatter, music halts, and the green lanterns burn steadily overhead, their flames flickering in rhythm with the laughter now echoing through the city.

data.name: The Crimson Harvest
data.description: [PvP, Wartorn Battleground | limited window]. The House does not take from its guests. Bloodflower grows where the ground has stopped draining, and the Battleground is the only place it grows at all. Eight fights, one cutting, and the House pays in vintage.
data.successDescription: The cask goes down the stair and the House forgets your face, which is the service you were actually paid for.

objectives.description: The Herald receives you at the service gate rather than the front, which tells you exactly which half of tonight you have been hired for. The House needs bloodflower cut from the Battleground while the ball is loud enough to cover the errand, and needs it cut by hands nobody upstairs will recognise later.
Eight fights, and the sector pays its own way before the House pays anything. Start where the ground is already wet.
objectives.successDescription: Two. Nothing there drains, and the field is a little louder for it.

objectives.description: The Battleground does not settle after a fight so much as absorb it, and bloodflower comes up wherever the ground has taken the most. The Herald was specific: cut what has opened tonight, leave the rest to come back.
Cut bloodflower where the fighting has been thickest longest. The stems fill a cask slowly, and the sector does not stop being the sector while you kneel in it.
objectives.successDescription: One bloodflower, cut and cased. The House will have the rest of it out of the stems by morning.

objectives.description: A runner from the House finds you before the strap is tight. The Herald has revised the order upward, as the Herald tends to, and offers nothing by way of explanation beyond the observation that the evening is running longer than planned.
Three more. The sector has begun to notice that someone is working it on a schedule.
objectives.successDescription: Five. Word travels in a place this small, and you are now part of what travels.

objectives.description: You are being watched now, which was always going to happen and is not, strictly speaking, a problem. The Herald's instructions covered this in a single line: finish the count.
The last three, and these ones will see you coming.
objectives.successDescription: Eight. The order is filled and the ground is done giving.

objectives.description: The Cellarer meets you at the head of the stair rather than letting you down it. The House settles outside accounts in vintage, one cask, drawn from whichever cellar you name, and the naming is the only part of this arrangement you have ever been offered a say in.
Drawn from the deep cellar, where the casks sit in packed earth and come up tasting of the ground they waited in. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the flooded cellar, where the casks float on their tethers and knock together all night. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the high cellar, where the casks are kept under copper and the air tastes of coming weather. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the kiln cellar, where the casks are turned beside banked coals and the seals are wax that has softened twice. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.
Drawn from the open cellar, where the casks are cured in a draught that never stops moving. The Cellarer does not thank you. The Cellarer never does.

data.name: The Last Shadow
data.description: Raizen Kurogane has escaped Blackstone Detention Fortress. Join the Global ANBU pursuit and uncover why a legendary prisoner is running toward the edge of the world.
data.successDescription: The pursuit reaches the Valley of Echoes, where Raizen's true destination waits beneath ancient chains.

objectives.description: Commander Kael: “Raizen Kurogane has escaped Blackstone Fortress. Every nation believes him to be the world's most dangerous criminal. Find him before whatever he's planning reaches its end.”
Investigate Blackstone Detention Fortress for evidence of Raizen's escape.
objectives.successDescription: Broken sealing chains and destroyed prison barriers reveal a carefully planned escape rather than a reckless breakout.

objectives.description: System Narration: “Every prison seal was broken with precision. Raizen left no unnecessary destruction and harmed none of the prison staff.”
Follow Raizen's trail through abandoned safehouses scattered across the frozen border.
objectives.successDescription: Cold campfires and abandoned shelters suggest Raizen is constantly moving while avoiding unnecessary conflict.

objectives.description: Four rogue mercenaries descend on the watchtower, intending to claim Raizen and silence the pursuing ANBU.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ends without containment.
objectives.failDescription: Your formation breaks beneath the enemy assault.
objectives.fleeDescription: You retreat before the objective is secured.
objectives.successDescription: The surviving mercenaries reveal that Raizen repeatedly refused to kill anyone pursuing him.

objectives.description: Commander Kael: “He could have slaughtered every squad we've sent. Instead, he leaves them alive. Either he's mocking us… or he's trying to save time.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Then we reach the valley before time runs out.

objectives.description: System Narration: “Your hesitation costs the pursuit its only remaining lead. Far beneath the Valley of Echoes, the first ancient chain breaks.”
The mercenaries scatter the pursuit. Regroup at the Frozen Borderlands and intercept them again.
The trail points unmistakably toward the Valley of Echoes.

🚨 EMERGENCY DISPATCH

PRIORITY: S-CLASS THREAT — SIEGE PROTOCOL

  • Unpredictable Aggression: Alternating between hiding and sudden chakra bursts when startled.
  • Innate Chakra Use: Uncontrolled nature chakra breath; not focused — causes violent plant eruptions. Highly volatile.

data.name: Larry's Undertow
data.description: Larry has a game: three riddles down, treasure up. Where you surface decides what you carry out.
data.successDescription: You surfaced from Larry's game with the sea's payment in hand.

objectives.description: Larry flags you down from a barrel-top perch. "Evening, swimmer. Fancy a game? Three riddles down, treasure up. One rule I give free: the deep don't shout."
"Three currents leave this harbor. One runs loud over the rocks. One runs wide and easy. One runs under, where the light don't follow. Which do you swim?"

nextObjectiveId.text: The loud one, over the rocks.

objectives.description: "The rocks sing when the tide turns, and a wreck sits on them, hull full of cargo. What do you do?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Strip the cargo before the tide turns.
Turn back. Rocks are no place for a boat.
Wait for the tide to lift her free.

objectives.description: "Storm's coming and your net is full. What's the move?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Haul it in fast, before the storm hits.
Cut the net loose and run.
Ride it out. The catch isn't going anywhere.

objectives.description: "It is dark down here. Something big passes overhead. What do you do?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Strike first, before it sees you.
Hold still and let it pass.

objectives.description: "The tide lifts the wreck and her cargo is yours. The rocks kept one chest back. How hard do you pull?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Break the hull for the last chest.
Take what came free and go.
Leave it. The rocks earned their keep.

objectives.description: "Storm's passed. Your net held, and then some: a second net drifted in, someone else's, still full. What now?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the fish, leave the net.
Cut it free to drift home.

objectives.description: "So you found the under-road. The Sea-King will see you now. What do you ask of him?"
"Turning tail already? The sea keeps what you leave behind. Swim back and think slower."
"You want nothing. Then everything is yours, swimmer. The Sea-King grants you audience."
"A seat at the Sea-King's table. You swam it clean."
"The deep current carried you fair. Fair is still good eating."
"The shallows for you tonight. Greed swims heavy. Come back slower tomorrow."

data.name: Ghost Ship: Pirate King(Gather)
data.description: Board the Ghost Ship and defeat the Pirate King for a chance to find buried treasure.

objectives.description: The ghost ship crosses the moon trailing green fire, and the sea goes quiet beneath it. Tonight it anchors close enough to board. Choose your way in.

nextObjectiveId.text: Hail the ship and ask for parley

objectives.description: The Ghostly Bosun waits at the top of the gangplank with the deck watch, powder crates stacked at the rail behind him. He does not ask your business.
Break the deck watch: the Ghostly Bosun and his powder stores.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The cold water takes you and the ship waits, patient as the tide. Board again.
Climb the anchor chain hand over hand before the watch turns. Gather your footing on the wet iron links.
You slip through the hull breach into the bilge, ankle-deep in black water. Something vast unfolds from the weed-wrapped timbers: the Ghostly Bilge Horror.
The Ghostly Bilge Horror rises from the black water.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Horror drags you under the black water and feeds you back out the breach. Climb again.

A tall figure of pale lantern light salutes from the rail: the Ghostly Herald. 'Answer true and walk aboard oathbound. Answer false and answer my blade. What does every sailor keep that the sea always takes?'
'True.' The Herald steps aside and the crew parts before you, all the way to the helm. 'You walk aboard oathbound. The King will know.'
'False.' The Herald draws a slender dueling blade and salutes. 'Then the duel is your answer.'
The Ghostly Herald salutes and begins the duel.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Herald's blade finds you three times and he lets the sea take you, unimpressed. Hail the ship again.
The deck stretches impossibly wide under tattered black sails. Three ways forward: the chart-lit captain's quarters, the stairs down to the gold-breathing hold, or the long walk to the helm.
The Ghostly Navigator looks up from charts of impossible seas, ink swirling off his hands like living shadow. The coded map you need hangs at his belt.
The Ghostly Navigator redraws the room around you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: Ink and shadow blind you, and you wake back on the deck. The quarters wait.
You cut the coded map free. Landmarks you know, drawn wrong on purpose, and a riddle inked along the margin. The dig site is out there under the moon.
Drifts of gold coin rise taller than a man. The Ghostly Quartermaster steps between you and the crates, coin-weighted maul on his shoulder, ledger chained to his belt. 'Nothing leaves unaccounted.'
The Ghostly Quartermaster hefts the coin-weight maul.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The maul writes you into the ledger and the hold spits you out. Descend again.
The King's retinue holds the helm: two Ghostly Bosuns stand side by side before a crowned throne of ship timber, mirror-perfect down to the knots in their lashes.
The retinue bars the last steps to the throne.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The retinue holds and the helm stays the King's. Walk it again.
Even the oathbound walk through the retinue. Two Ghostly Bosuns bar the last steps to the throne, and neither bows.
The retinue bars the way, oath or no oath.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The retinue holds, oath or no oath. Walk it again.
The margin riddle reads: 'Where the cliff drinks and the stone watches, dig beneath the watcher's shadow.' Three coves lie under the moon.

The open beach past the reef

objectives.description: You dig until your arms burn. Rusted cutlasses, crab shells, no chest. The watcher's shadow falls elsewhere.
Sand and reef and nothing buried but a dead man's anchor. Read the riddle again.
Dig beneath the stone watcher's shadow before the tide turns.
Your shovel strikes iron, and the beach itself stands up. The Ghostly Guardian erupts from the sand, shell and reef spike crouched around your prize.
The Ghostly Guardian erupts from the sand.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Guardian buries you to the neck and settles back over the chest. The dig site remains.
The Guardian collapses into wet sand and the chest beneath is iron-bound and heavy with promise. X marks the spot.
You read the dead man's map true and took the treasure from the sand itself.
The hold is yours. Crates you can carry sit in the open. Behind them, a black iron vault hums with something worse. Fortune favors the brave.

nextObjectiveId.text: Grab what you can carry and go

objectives.description: You shoulder a crate and make for the gangplank. The Ghostly Bosun stands at the rail one last time, hook in hand.
The Bosun bars the gangplank one last time.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Bosun hooks you back aboard by the collar. The rail is right there.
You spill onto the beach with your crate as the ship slides back into the dark. A modest haul, and your neck intact.
Not every fortune is worth the vault that guards it. You took the sure thing.
The lock breaks and the hold goes cold. The Ghostly First Mate steps out of the vault's dark behind twin gale cleavers, coat snapping in a wind that should not exist below decks.
The Ghostly First Mate steps out of the vault's dark.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The storm folds you in half and the vault seals itself to wait. Crack it again.
The storm dies with him. The vault stands open, and what the King hid from his own crew is yours.
You woke what greed keeps chained and beat it anyway. Fortune favors the brave.
The Pirate King rises from the crowned throne, green fire guttering along his cutlass. 'Bold. The sea remembers bold.'
The Pirate King rises from the crowned throne.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The King breaks you against the wheel and the crew throws you to the sea, laughing. The helm waits.
The King kneels, green fire dying along the blade. 'Take it, then. Three hundred years I gathered it for someone worth losing to.'
You walked the longest deck straight to the throne and took the hoard from the King himself.
The King rises, and the Herald's word arrives before you do. 'Oathbound. Then you get the King the crew remembers.' The green fire around him turns white.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face the King at his full fury

objectives.description: The green fire turns white. The King the crew remembers steps down from the throne.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The enraged King breaks you against the wheel, then waits for the sigil to knit you back together. An oathbound duel does not end until one of you yields. He has not.

The white fire dies and the King kneels, laughing through broken teeth. 'Oath kept.' He presses the hoard's key into your hand himself. The best of his treasure was always reserved for the one who earned it.
You answered true, dueled with honor, and broke the King at his strongest. No richer night exists aboard the Ghost Ship.

data.name: The Crimson Bloom
data.description: The riverside village of Clearwater is suffering from the "Burning Fever," a strange ailment causing high fevers, aggression, and eventual exhaustion. As a medical specialist, you must investigate the mysterious illness, correctly deduce the components for a cure through a series of clinical judgments, and synthesize the antidote before the village succumbs to the madness.
data.successDescription: The elixir works. The villagers' fevers break, and the aggressive rage subsides, replaced by a peaceful calm. Your sharp medical mind has brought peace and healing to Clearwater.

objectives.description: Our people are consumed by the Burning Fever! They are aggressive, paranoid, and then they just... collapse. We need a true healer, someone who can see the root of this madness.

You examine a patient. Their body is burning with fever, and their chakra is flaring in uncontrolled, violent bursts. It's not a subtle decay; it's a system in overdrive. What is your initial diagnosis?

Hyper-stimulation? That explains the rage. But how? I've noticed the villagers who work closest to the river—the fishermen and launderers—were the first to fall ill. What is your next investigative step?
Your deduction points to the river. You follow a small tributary upstream to find the source of the contamination.
You find the source: a vibrant crimson flower growing into the creek. You collect a petal for analysis.

The petal radiates a powerful, stimulating energy. It's a biological accelerant, forcing the chakra system into a dangerous, feverish state. To create the cure, you must calm this raging fire. What is the correct medical strategy?
To find a natural suppressant, you need a low-energy, calming environment. A dark, quiet cave would be the ideal place to look.
Inside the quiet grotto, you find a patch of pale, bioluminescent fungi. You collect a cap.

You have the stimulant and the suppressant. However, their opposing energies are too potent; they will neutralize each other violently if mixed. You need a third ingredient to act as a binding agent, to stabilize the volatile reaction. What kind of ingredient should you look for?

You have all three components. Using the Ironwood Fiber to bind the opposing energies of the bloom and the fungus, you successfully synthesize a stable, cooling elixir. You have crafted the Feverbane Elixir
Return to Clearwater Village to administer the cure.

You administer the elixir. The villagers' fevers break, and the aggressive rage in their eyes fades, replaced by a peaceful calm. "You... you did it," Jin says, relief washing over him. "You calmed the fire. Thank you."

And when the tags start singing, put four of the responders in the dirt. You'll be deep in enemy ground with a mark on your back the whole time. Come home anyway."
Plant the explosive tags on the enemy munitions depot.
The tags hum against the depot wall, ink glowing faintly in the dark. Somewhere above, a patrol whistle rises. They know. Four of them now stand between you and the border.
Defeat four enemy shinobi on their home ground.

You cross the border with patrol whistles fading behind you. By the time you reach the hall, Okabe has already marked four lines in the ledger. "Their patrols double tonight. That's the arithmetic of fear."
Mission complete.

data.name: The Silent Bloom
data.description: The secluded village of Verdant Hollow is afflicted by the "Ashen Slumber," a mysterious condition where villagers fall into a deep, unwaking sleep. As a medical specialist, you must use your diagnostic and analytical skills to investigate the cause, deduce the necessary components for a cure, and synthesize an elixir before the slumber becomes permanent.
data.successDescription: The elixir works. A wave of gentle energy washes over the village, and the sleeping residents begin to stir, awakening as if from a long dream. Your medical expertise and sharp investigative mind have saved Verdant Hollow.

objectives.description: Our people are falling into the Ashen Slumber. Our healers are baffled. Please, use your skills to diagnose this illness and find a cure. The fate of our village is in your hands.

Your diagnostic jutsu reveals no cellular decay from poison and no residual energy from genjutsu. The patients' life signs are stable but incredibly slow, as if their entire metabolism has been put on hold. What is your primary diagnosis?
Stasis? A forced hibernation? The only recent change was a strong northern wind carrying a sweet scent. The water tastes the same, the ground is unchanged. What is your next investigative step?
Based on your deduction, you travel to the Whispering Canyon to find the source of the airborne agent.
The canyon is filled with a fine, grey pollen. A Spore-Infused Boar, made aggressive by the spores, charges at you
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You find the source: a pale, shade-loving flower, the Ashen Lotus. You carefully collect a sample of its potent pollen.
You analyze the pollen. It induces a state of extreme lethargy by calming chakra to a near-standstill. To create an antidote, you must reverse this process. What is the correct medical strategy?

To counteract the calming effect, you need a natural ingredient with intensely stimulating properties, likely one that thrives in a high-energy environment. Your map shows a location that fits the criteria: the Sunstone Mesa.
On the sun-baked surface of the mesa, you find a patch of vibrant ferns that seem to glow with absorbed sunlight.

You now have two highly reactive, opposing ingredients. Combining them directly will result in a volatile, uncontrolled energy release. What is the correct synthesis process to create a stable elixir?
You deduce that you need a pure, liquid medium. Elder Kaelen mentioned a sacred spring blessed by the village's founder. Travel there.

You have all three components. Following your deductions, you use the pure water as a medium to balance the two opposing ingredients. The mixture stabilizes, glowing with a warm, golden light. You have successfully crafted Anya's Wakefulness Elixir.

nextObjectiveId.text: Return to Verdant Hollow to administer the cure

objectives.description: Return to Verdant Hollow to administer the cure.

You administer the elixir. A golden light spreads from person to person, and slowly, the villagers begin to awaken. Elder Kaelen weeps with joy. "Your skill is beyond anything I have ever seen. You have saved us all."
Your deduction was flawed. Unable to correctly identify the cause or the necessary components, you cannot create the cure. The Ashen Slumber remains, and the village is lost to its silent fate.

objectives.description: Ren returns steadier, promoted in expectation if not yet in certainty. The Lower District reports forbidden chakra stimulants.
Go to the Lower District infirmary and question the Genin who bought strength.
The hospitalized Genin admits he bought the drug because he was falling behind clan-born students.
Ren watches the boy breathe easier. 'Weakness is not always failure. Sometimes it is a wound.'
Ren's jaw tightens. 'If wanting power ruins you, maybe ruin is the price of being weak.'
Ren nods. 'Mercy can be a negotiation. He lives, and the truth moves.'
Ren looks at the chart beside the bed. 'Shame opens mouths faster than kindness.'
Follow the names to the illegal clinic where black water stimulants are refined.
Subdue the clinic sentinel before the rogue medical-nin destroys the patient ledger.

objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The clinic locks down. Regroup outside the black water drain and enter again.
The rogue medical-nin claims Wake Island created the demand by favoring the gifted and abandoning the rest.

nextObjectiveId.text: Spare the medic if they treat victims.
Take the research for Wake Island.

objectives.description: Ren looks over the broken vials. 'A dangerous system should not be managed. It should end.'
Ren studies the medic's shaking hands. 'Redemption can have conditions.'
Ren closes the ledger. 'Power should not be wasted just because dirty hands found it first.'
Ren's voice drops. 'Controlled corruption is still control.'
Bring the ledger to the Tidebreaker Candidate Yard, where a rival waits in the rain.
The rival candidate accuses Ren of being protected. End the challenge before it becomes a riot.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The candidate yard turns against you. Pull Ren out and face the rival again.
The rival says Ren only advances because you protect them. Ren looks shaken for the first time in months.

nextObjectiveId.text: Recruit the rival as an informant.

objectives.description: Ren's eyes soften. 'You did not have to stand between me and their words. You did anyway.'
Ren steps forward. 'My strength has to be mine when you are not there.'
Ren watches the crowd turn. 'Dominance protects reputation faster than truth.'
Ren tilts their head. 'An enemy can become a tool before they become a friend.'
Present the stimulant ledger to Wake Island command under black rain.
The ledger proves instructors ignored the stimulant trade because it produced stronger candidates.
Ren looks toward the gathered candidates. 'Truth can break a hall and still be worth speaking.'
Ren folds the ledger. 'Justice can be selective if the village survives.'
Ren's promotion badge feels heavy. 'Institutions are people too, just harder to mourn.'
Ren reads the names aloud, then chooses what Wake Island is allowed to know. Their voice does not shake.
After the hearing, Ren stares at the Global ANBU mask display and asks if truth can become an enemy.
Ren touches the glass. 'Then a village that cannot survive truth was already bleeding.'
Ren nods slowly. 'A blade in the open causes panic. A blade in the dark ends the threat.'
Ren turns away from the mask. 'Then the program exists for candidates, not the other way around.'
Ren's reflection overlaps the mask. 'Peace may need someone willing to be misunderstood.'
Ren earns Chunin recognition beneath black rain, and begins applying your values without asking.

data.name: One Perfect Crop
data.successDescription: Ittetsu and the shipment reached their destination. What happened after that is, thankfully, the market's problem.

objectives.description:
A cabbage cart sits crooked beside the country road, one wheel split clean through and half its belongings scattered into the grass. A farmer is already gathering tools and checking the lashings around an improbably healthy mound of cabbages.

"If you're a shinobi, I could use another pair of hands. I'm Ittetsu. This harvest is expected at market before the day is out."

"The cart was fine this morning. Then a passing wagon threw one stone into exactly the wrong pin, and here we are."

Before lifting the last tool back onto the cart, Ittetsu tucks a small folded seed packet securely into his tool roll.

nextObjectiveId.text: Help him get the shipment to market.

objectives.description:
"I can repair the wheel properly, but it will take time."

Ittetsu checks the broken rim, then the road ahead. The cart can be made sound again if you stop here and do the job right. Or the good timber can be stripped down into a rough drag-sled and the shipment can start moving immediately.

nextObjectiveId.text: Strip it down. We keep moving.
Take the time to repair it properly.

objectives.description:
Ittetsu breaks down the damaged wheel, using the sound timber and ironwork to brace a crude sled. It is ugly, but it is ready now.

"Good enough."

"We can replace a cart. We cannot replace the hours."

Ittetsu works carefully. By the time the wheel is straight and the axle turns cleanly, the cart is in excellent shape again.

"There. That will hold."

The repair is good. The day, however, has kept moving.

The repaired cart reaches the river crossing intact. The Waystation Keeper is already chaining the loading gate shut while brown water climbs the pilings below.

"You just missed the final loaded crossing. River rose faster than expected. Nothing with cargo goes over until it settles."

"A good cart. Shame it cannot swim."

nextObjectiveId.text: There is no way to reach market in time.

objectives.description:
"Last loaded crossing of the day. Water is climbing, so I'm taking half the usual weight and twice the usual trouble."

The fee for the cabbage shipment will empty Ittetsu's purse and cost most of the provisions strapped to the sled. A free levee road follows the river toward market, longer but still apparently passable.

Ittetsu counts out every coin, then adds his packed provisions when the Waystation Keeper points out the remaining weight allowance. By the time the shipment crosses, he has little left besides his tools and the clothes on his back.

"Expensive crossing."

"You could have taken the levee."

"I could also have eaten my money. Neither gets the harvest to market."

For a while, the old levee road seems like the smarter choice. It is quiet, dry, and empty enough that the loaded cart makes better time than expected.

"We are still moving. I'll call that good news while it lasts."

A lone shinobi steps from the trees ahead and plants himself in the middle of the levee. His attention settles immediately on the loaded shipment.

"Toll road is for travelers with money. This road is for travelers with something worth taking."

"I already dislike this road."

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The Road Bandit retreats, leaving the road open. Ittetsu checks every rope, every bundle, and finally the cabbages themselves.

"Nothing missing. Keep moving."

The road stays peaceful long enough for the fight to feel like the only danger it had to offer. Then somewhere upstream, wood cracks with a sound like a tree splitting.

"That was not a tree."

An irrigation gate gives way upstream, sending a sudden wall of water across the low levee. Ittetsu gets clear, but the loaded cart is swept sideways into the flooded channels before either of you can secure it.

"I can repair a cart. I can earn more coin. I cannot sell a harvest that is halfway to the coast."

Beyond the crossing, the route climbs between terraced fields. A section of old retaining wall suddenly gives way, knocking Ittetsu beneath a broken fence rail as the loaded sled shifts sideways on the sloping road.

"Well. That's unfortunate."

The rail is pressing harder against Ittetsu, while the sled gives another slow scrape toward the edge of the drainage cut.

You catch the sled before it reaches the edge and drive its brace into the road. With the shipment secure, it takes only moments to lift the rail and drag Ittetsu free.

"Good choice. I was not going anywhere. The harvest was."

He tests his leg, finds it usable, and immediately reaches for the hauling rope.

You pull Ittetsu free before the fallen stones can shift again. The rescue works perfectly.

"The load."

The sled is already in the drainage cut. You recover what you can, but too much of the harvest is crushed, soaked, or scattered to fulfill the delivery.

"You saved me."

"I wish the cabbages could say the same."

nextObjectiveId.text: The shipment can no longer be delivered.

objectives.description:
The market road is finally visible ahead when one side restraint snaps loose. A single flawless cabbage slips free, bounces once, and begins rolling toward the irrigation ditch below.

Ittetsu freezes.

"No-no, not that one."

For the first time all day, real alarm enters his voice.

"That was the best head in the whole harvest."

Behind you, the main load shifts with a long wooden creak. One of the remaining ropes is sliding steadily through its knot. Nothing else has fallen yet.

Ittetsu looks from the runaway cabbage to the load.

"...Damn it."

You seize the slipping rope and haul the main load back into place. Below, the perfect cabbage rolls through the grass and disappears into the irrigation ditch.

Ittetsu watches it go.

"...That was a beautiful cabbage."

He tightens the rope beside you, still staring downhill.

"But one cabbage is not a harvest."

"Keep moving."

You sprint downhill and catch the runaway cabbage just before it reaches the water. It is completely unharmed.

When you turn around, the main load is gone.

"Excellent catch."

"Now where is the rest?"

nextObjectiveId.text: One perfect cabbage is not the shipment.

objectives.description:
The shipment is secure again, and the market gate is close enough to hear carts and vendors beyond it. For the first time since meeting Ittetsu, the road ahead looks almost uneventful.

"Do not say anything."

The brush beside the road explodes outward. A large wild boar barrels through the fence, catches the scent of fresh produce, and immediately turns toward the loaded shipment.

"Of course."

The boar lowers its head and charges.

"That one wants the load. Drive it off."

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description:
The Harvest Boar finally turns and crashes back through the brush. Ittetsu checks the load, tightens one rope, and points toward the market gate.

"Good. Keep moving before the sky learns what we're carrying."

The battered shipment rolls into market looking as though it has survived a small war. A Market Clerk watches Ittetsu approach, looks at the cabbages, then looks back at Ittetsu.

"Ittetsu."

"Count them."

The Market Clerk inspects the surviving load, checks the delivery slate, and marks the shipment received.

"Shipment accepted. Your delivery is complete."

"Complete?"

"Complete."

Ittetsu stares at the accepted shipment for several seconds. His shoulders finally drop.

"There."

"Done."

A sudden gust catches a market awning and tears one support loose. The falling pole startles a pack animal, which kicks an empty handcart downhill into the newly accepted cabbage stack.

The stack collapses. Cabbages scatter across the market, bounce down the sloping street, and pour almost ceremonially into the drainage canal.

"MY CABBAGES!"

When the noise finally stops, Ittetsu finds his battered tool roll beneath an overturned basket. The folded seed packet inside has been torn open, but one seed remains caught in the paper crease.

"It was received before all this. The mark on the slate stands."

"Yes."

data.name: The Crimson Masquerade
data.description: A blood-court ball in a manor that appears only on moonless nights. All are invited. Few are announced.

objectives.description: The manor stands where no manor stood yesterday, every window burning candle-gold. A queue of masked guests waits at the door, and the garden wall is dark.

nextObjectiveId.text: Present yourself at the front door
Approach the Herald of the House
Linger by the queue and listen

objectives.description: A drunk viscount is retelling his rejection to anyone who will hear. 'I told the Herald WINE. Wine! What else does a host drink? And the doors stayed shut.' His companion murmurs: a host serves. A host does not partake.

nextObjectiveId.text: Present yourself at the front door
Approach the Herald of the House

objectives.description: The Doorman fills the doorway entirely. Two candelabra drift from their sconces and take up position at his shoulders. 'Invitations,' he says, 'or entertainment.'
The Doorman and his candelabra bar the way.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Doorman sets you back on the gravel almost gently. The queue applauds.
The briars on the garden wall are older than they look and less asleep. Climb fast and do not let go.
You drop into the service yard. The coal chute stands open, and something that was poured down it long ago climbs back out to meet you.
The Cellar Thing drags itself into the candlelight.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Thing folds you over the wall and back into the briars. The manor's windows flicker, amused.
The Herald of the House regards you over a raised finger. 'One question, as is custom. What does the Count drink at his own ball?'

nextObjectiveId.text: Blood. Everyone knows what he is
Nothing. The host serves; he does not partake

objectives.description: 'Wine.' The Herald's smile does not move. 'The cellars hold ten thousand bottles and the Count has opened none of them. You may enter the way the uninvited enter.'
'How vulgar,' the Herald says, delighted. 'And how wrong. The Count has better manners than his reputation. You may enter the way the uninvited enter.'
The Herald of the House draws a thin blade with ceremony.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Herald dusts you off and returns you to the gravel. 'Do think on the question.'
The Herald bows low. 'The host serves.' The doors open themselves, and your name, somehow, is announced correctly. You enter as an Invited Guest.

The Doorman's wing swallows you: service passages, the glint of the untended silver, the cellar stair breathing cold, and beyond it all the grand stair. The doors close behind you. The evening is chosen.

nextObjectiveId.text: Pocket the silverware and slip out

objectives.description: You are inside the way the staff are inside: unannounced, unwatched, and holding the servants' keys. The hedge maze glows through the service windows, the cellar door stands ajar, and the gallery corridor runs dark and empty. The evening is chosen.

nextObjectiveId.text: The Hedge Maze, through the service door

objectives.description: The whisper settles into memory: she leads. She always leads. The music turns you back toward the evening.

The ballroom parts for the Invited Guest. The Countess is already watching you across the floor, the gallery glows with candled portraits, and the grand stair stands unbarred by pretense. The evening is chosen.

nextObjectiveId.text: Linger among the dancers and listen

objectives.description: A pale servant refills your glass without being asked and says nothing at all. Nearby, two dancers whisper: the Countess only dances the old form. She leads. She always leads.

nextObjectiveId.text: Return your attention to the evening

objectives.description: The service table gleams. The silverware is heavy, old, and unattended. Almost unattended. The Doorman is watching you from the doorway with something like respect.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take it and go through him

objectives.description: The Doorman blocks the servants' exit. 'House property,' he says. 'Mostly the House's.'
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: He takes the silverware back and pats your shoulder. The ballroom pretends not to have seen.
You are over the wall with the House's silver. Threaded through the bundle, finer than any fork: silver thread, spun for the court's own dress.

The Portrait Gallery is longer than the manor is wide, and the Curator's rounds allow you time for exactly one indulgence before he notices you: the discarded dance card, the servants' argument, or the portrait whose mask is not painted.

nextObjectiveId.text: Listen to the two servants arguing
Study the portrait with the real mask
Ignore it all and announce yourself to the Curator

objectives.description: A dance card in the Countess's hand, discarded: 'The bow, met depth for depth. The turn, surrendered. The question, answered in service.' Court shorthand, but legible.
Two servants argue in fierce whispers. 'The kneeling maiden was moved to the east corner last winter, I carried her myself.' 'You carried the piper.' 'The MAIDEN.'
The Curator turns. 'Guests view the collection. They do not join it. Usually.'
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You wake propped against the wall like an exhibit. The Curator has straightened your collar.
Behind the largest frame: a coded invitation, decades old. 'The garden remembers. Dig where the maiden kneels.' The hedge maze waits below the terrace, its statues patient.

nextObjectiveId.text: Dig beneath the kneeling maiden, east corner

objectives.description: The earth beneath the piper is empty and offended. Somewhere in the hedges, something large turns over in its sleep.
The lions guard nothing but roots. The hedge walls seem a step closer than they were.
You slip back to the terrace with dirt on your gloves and nothing to show.
You slip back to the terrace with dirt on your gloves and nothing to show.
The earth beneath the kneeling maiden is soft, as if dug before and asked to keep the secret. Work quickly. The hedges are listening.
The hedge walls knit shut behind you. What you took from the earth, the garden means to take back, and the topiary at the maze's heart opens two ember eyes.
The Garden Sentinel rises, wearing the maze itself as armor.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The hedges deposit you at the maze mouth, politely, the way one returns a borrowed book.
The maze lets you leave with your prize: bone beads, carved from something the garden buried long before the manor learned to appear.
The portrait's mask is real: a dead noble's face, waiting for a new wearer. The frame's brass plate reads HOUSE VELOCE. Beneath, someone has scratched: the '43, and none for himself.
The mask resists like something being woken. Work it loose before the Curator's rounds return.
Wearing the dead noble's face, you join the receiving line. The Herald asks, as form requires: 'Your house words?'

nextObjectiveId.text: House Veloce, in blood and candlelight

objectives.description: The Herald inclines his head. A steward offers the tray: 'And the vintage the House prefers?'

'The '43.' The steward's eyes shine. You are announced as an honored guest to general applause. But at the door, as you leave laden with the House's gifts, the hounds rise: the House never lets a borrowed face leave.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face the hounds before the whole ballroom

objectives.description: A pause. The steward's smile becomes fixed. You make your exit early, but in the long corridor the candles gutter, and the mask slips, and the hounds are already there.
The House's hounds circle with courtly patience while the ballroom watches.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The hounds have you cornered in the corridor, and no one is watching at all.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The hounds escort you, breathing smoke, back to the receiving line. The Herald pretends the interruption never happened.
You wake in the corridor with the mask askew and your dignity elsewhere.
You leave as the House's honored guest, a gilded clasp pinned at your shoulder by the Herald himself.
You leave through a window with a gilded clasp pried from a hound's collar, which counts.
The cellar stair descends past ten thousand bottles. The Cellarer waits at the ledger desk, quill moving, counting what you have not yet taken.

nextObjectiveId.text: Pause where the pale servant is drawing a vintage

objectives.description: The pale servant draws a single glass of the '43, sets it on a silver tray, and pours it out onto the stones. An offering, or a habit. He bows fractionally and says nothing.
The Cellarer sets down his quill. 'Everything that leaves this cellar is paid for. Everything.'
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You are carried up the stair and entered into the ledger under DECLINED.
Below the wine is an older cellar, its casks marked with names instead of years. Something in the deep dark has been the Warden of it for a very long time.
The Cellar Warden steps out of the dark between one candle and the next.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Warden returns you to the wine cellar and rolls a cask against the lower door.
From the Warden's hoard: a blood-garnet bead, warm as a held hand, cut for a rosary the House prefers to forget.
Two Doormen bar the grand stair, mirror-perfect down to the crease of their gloves. Above, a door stands open on candlelight.
The Doormen advance in step.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Doormen return you to the ballroom floor with professional courtesy.
The Count rises from a chair by the fire, all grace and candle-gold. 'A guest with ambition. How the evening improves.' He does not reach for a weapon. He does not appear to need one.

nextObjectiveId.text: Give him the fight he is smiling about

objectives.description: The Count is gracious to the last. The last is now.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You wake on the landing, straightened and dusted, a glass of the '43 set beside you untouched.
The Count concedes the evening with a bow and presses a moonstone bead into your palm. 'For the rosary. You will want the rest.'
The Doormen bow to the Invited Guest, and bar the stair anyway. 'Forgive us. Even invitation is tested here.'
The Doormen test the invitation thoroughly.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Doormen set you down in the ballroom. 'The invitation stands. The stair, also.'

The Count receives his invited guest by the tall windows. 'You answered truly. Then you have earned the truth.' The candles gutter as one. The mask comes away, and the light through the windows turns moon-silver.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face what the mask was for

objectives.description: The Count Unmasked fills the room with silver light and a very old thirst.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: You wake in the ballroom below. Above, the tall windows burn silver, patient as the moon.
From the unmasked Count's own rosary, broken across the floor: the Seventh Bead, moon-silver and humming faintly, the centerpiece the others remember.
The Countess's hand is cool as the far side of a pillow. The old form begins with the bow, and hers is already falling, precise as a verdict.

nextObjectiveId.text: Do not bow. You are equals

objectives.description: The turn. Her hand tightens by a feather's weight, a question in pressure: who leads?
Close now, past the reach of the music, she asks the only question the House ever asks: 'Why did you come?'
Her smile opens like a knife drawer. 'Every step true. You dance well enough to die well.' The music stops. The floor clears. This is also part of the old form.
The music sours by a half-step only you and she can hear. She finishes the dance with cold correctness and steps back. 'Adequate,' she says, drawing her blade. 'The floor is yours to be adequate on.'
The Countess duels the way she dances: delighted, and leading.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Countess duels without interest, which is worse.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: She helps you up herself. 'Again, someday. You very nearly died beautifully.'
A servant helps you up. The Countess is already dancing with someone else.
She unpins a silk ribbon from her gown and ties it around your wrist herself. 'For the sash. Wear it where the Count can see.'
A silk ribbon torn free in the duel, still cold from her hand.

data.name: Mountain Madness
data.description:
The medical unit has been working really hard lately! But suddenly there’s a new illness sweeping its way through the village and no one has been able to come up with a treatment. It started after a small group of villagers returned from a hunting party that came back from a hunt up in the mountains a few days ago.
Can you head over there and see if they need a hand?
data.successDescription: You create the perfect cure! But how did the plant get here from all the way up in the mountains..

objectives.description: Thank you for coming. We’ve had an influx of reports on some strange illness that’s been plaguing the village. Ever since that group came back from the mountains something hasn’t felt right. It’s almost like they stumbled upon something they weren’t supposed to find..
Check on the patients

You examine the patient.
There’s a strange blueish liquid leaking from their eyes. Their very breath is visible, almost like a mist escaping from their mouths and noses with each breath. They can’t even remember where they are or where they’ve been. Whatever it is, it’s spreading fast! What should we do?

You take a sample of the blueish liquid and start running some tests on it and after a few minor explosions from mixing things together come to the conclusion that there must be something toxic traveling through the air. You’ll need to find the source before you can figure out more.
Investigate the village centre

In the centre of the village you find a strange looking plant. You aren’t sure what it is, but you know it doesn’t belong here. Its black roots go deep into the ground, the veins within the leaves are glowing, and there’s a thick black fog, similar to the mist coming from the patients mouths, coming from the centres of the dark red flowers.
You’ve removed the plant, but the sick villagers still need a tonic to treat them.
Head to the lab to do the dissection

nextObjectiveId.text: Time to work on the cure

objectives.description: Start to work on the cure.

You start working on a tonic to cure the villagers, but you are unsure what the final ingredient should be because this has never happened before so you find a book with a list of different treatments used all over Seichi. Which treatment should you base your cure on?

objectives.successDescription: You create the perfect cure! If only we knew where the plant came from..

objectives.description: You've done it! Time to put it to the test!

data.name: The Archive Remembers
data.description: A distortion in the chakra fields erased techniques from living memory. The Grand Archive keeps backups of the forgotten.
data.successDescription: The forgotten techniques are restored from the Archive's backups.

objectives.description: The Archivist looks up from a lectern of drifting glyphs. "You felt it too. A sudden distortion tore through the chakra fields last night, and techniques were ripped out of living memory. Names, forms, whole schools of practice, gone as if never written."

"Fortunately, forgetting is a thing the Archive refuses to do. Every technique ever practiced in Seichi leaves an imprint here. We keep backups of the forgotten, sealed in ink and patience. Hold still, this will take several unsealings."

The Archivist slides two lacquered cases across the lectern. "First, the event seals. The Cleave and the Hollow Veil were bound to scrolls, so the scrolls come back first. Break them open when you are ready."

The Archivist unseals a shelf of tide and current techniques. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Abyssal Surge, Amaterasu's Renewal, Aqua Dragon Barrage, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a rack of flame and ember forms. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Crimson Spires, Crimson Tides, Debilitating Sword Strike, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a drawer of stone and earthwork methods. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Echoing Rift, Eclipse Drain, Endless Drowning, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a case of storm and lightning practice. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Fireball, Gale Force Blast, Infernal Ascension, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a folio of wind and gale arts. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Lightning Flash Strike, Majestic Flame, Mizukumi, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a binding of shadow and eclipse work. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Purifying Wave, Shrapnel Clone Barrage, Stone Pillar Strike, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a tray of temple and spirit forms. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Tempest of Shadows, Thunder Chain Slash, Thunder’s Judgement, and their kin. Restored, as they were."

The Archivist unseals a final ledger of stray and singular techniques. Pages lift and settle into your hands as the knowledge returns. "Tides of Sovereignty, Tornado Vortex, Volt Fang, and their kin. Restored, as they were."
"That is the last of them. The distortion has passed, and the field holds. If anything else has slipped your mind, come back. The Archive remembers, even when Seichi forgets."
The Archive falls quiet as the last seal settles.

data.name: Ren of Wake Island I: The Genin Beneath the Tide
data.description: Ren, an impressionable Genin candidate, joins you to investigate missing ships, lantern smugglers, and the sea cave beneath Wake Island.
data.successDescription: Ren remains in the Tidebreaker Program, changed by the first lesson you gave them.

objectives.description: A Tidebreaker instructor assigns Ren to you at the Bureau. Ren bows too quickly and watches how you answer.
Travel with Ren to the Eastern Docks and inspect the missing cargo manifests.
The dockworker's hands shake. He knows more than he admits. Ren waits to see what kind of pressure you use.
Ren whispers, 'You did not even raise your voice, and he still talked. I did not know strength could look like that.'
Ren's eyes harden. 'He gave us what we needed. Maybe being feared is better than being respected.'
Ren nods from the rain shadow. 'Observation can cut deeper than threats.'
Ren stumbles at first, then steadies. 'You trusted me with the silence between answers. I will remember that.'
Follow the lantern marks to a warehouse where stolen supplies move under debt contracts.
Inside the warehouse, smugglers hide behind poor workers forced into crime. Ren studies where you place blame.

nextObjectiveId.text: Burn the warehouse as a warning.

objectives.description: Ren lowers their voice. 'Law first. Sympathy after. That is clean, even when it hurts.'
Ren looks relieved. 'Victims and predators can stand in the same room. Justice should know the difference.'
Ren watches the workers bargain for safety. 'Desperate people can become assets if someone gives them a price.'
Ren stares into the smoke. 'A message people fear is still a message they obey.'
Break the smuggler guard line before the warehouse alarm reaches the reef caves.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The warehouse fight collapses. Regroup with Ren at the lantern trail.
Descend through the tide tunnel toward the sea cave beneath the Red Reef.
Ren freezes when the cave ambusher lunges. Decide under pressure and survive the first true battle.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The Red Reef fight goes wrong. Pull Ren back to the tide tunnel and try again.
After the ambush, Ren cannot meet your eyes. The moment will become their first real lesson.
Ren clutches their sleeve. 'You moved before I could deserve it. Does that mean a teammate has value before they are useful?'
Ren swallows hard. 'No one can breathe for me. I understand.'
Ren's face goes still. 'So fear can be placed like a trap. Even mine.'
Ren bows until their hair hides their eyes. 'I will not freeze again. I will not be the weak point.'
Return to the Tidebreaker Bureau and report what the Red Reef concealed.
Command asks if Ren should remain in the Tidebreaker Program. Ren stands close enough to hear.

nextObjectiveId.text: Lie and say Ren was perfect.

objectives.description: Ren blinks through the rain. 'You did not hide what went wrong, but you did not throw me away either.'
Ren nods once. 'If shame makes me sharper, I will learn to carry it.'
Ren's smile is small and uncertain. 'A report can become armor, even when it is not true.'
Ren takes a breath. 'I was afraid. I acted late. I want another mission anyway.'
Outside, Ren asks what matters more: not feeling fear, or acting anyway?
Ren repeats the words like a hand seal. 'Acting anyway. Then courage is something you do, not something you wait to feel.'
Ren's expression closes. 'Then I will become someone fear cannot find.'
Ren looks back toward the reef. 'A frightened person sees details others miss. I can use that.'
Ren nods slowly. 'A leader carries the consequence after the fear has passed.'
Ren survives their first Tidebreaker mission and begins shaping a worldview from your example.

data.name: The Shattered Sakura: Part 3 - A Crossroads of Duty
data.description: Near Glacier's supposed safety, news arrives that the Iron Claw Clan is annihilating the Sakura Bloom survivors. Choose between the duty of protecting Princess Yumi and the desperate hope of returning her to her people.
data.successDescription: At the crossroads between obligation and hope, your choice determined both Princess Yumi's future and the legacy of the shattered Sakura Bloom Clan.

objectives.description:
Temporary Refuge — Forest Cave

Takashi, voice low: "We are nearing Glacier's outer patrols. Safety is almost within reach. Yumi has been speaking more, hasn't she? About our village. About the others. She carries such a heavy burden for one so young. Her father's orders are clear, but..."

He trails off. Princess Yumi sits beside the meager fire, clutching her mother's pin while its faint light trembles across the cave walls.

Temporary Refuge — Forest Cave

Princess Yumi looks up, her eyes no longer empty but burning with quiet resolve.

"I cannot abandon them. Our people… they suffer. Father made me leave for my protection, but what of their protection? The Iron Claw attacks. I carry Mama's pin now. It feels warm. It feels like strength. I must help them."

Takashi's jaw tightens. "Her spirit is strong. But her safety… that is our mission."

nextObjectiveId.text: We need more information before any decision.

objectives.description: Seek Kiyoshi at the Glacier scout rendezvous beside the frozen river.

Scout's Camp — Makeshift

Kiyoshi studies you over a frostglass map. "You're the escort. Good. The Iron Claw have begun a full-scale assault on the remaining Sakura Bloom settlements. Lord Genzo himself leads the charge. They intend to erase the clan and claim its ancestral lands."

Takashi pales. Yumi's grief flashes into fierce determination. "My people… under siege. I have to go back!"

Kiyoshi offers an ice-forged device. "This is a Glacier Rescue Beacon. Glacier is two days ahead. Your home is one hard day behind you. Duty, or a desperate hope—the choice is yours."

nextObjectiveId.text: I understand. Give me the beacon.

objectives.description: Receive Kiyoshi's single-use Glacier Rescue Beacon.

Scout's Camp — Makeshift

Yumi clasps her glowing pin. "Please! They are my people. Mama's spirit protects them too. I will not be safe knowing they are lost. Please—help me save them!"

Takashi stares into the fire. "My orders are to ensure her safety. But her spirit is undeniable. What say you, shinobi? Do we fulfill our oath and continue to Glacier, or turn back toward a battle we may not survive?"

nextObjectiveId.text: We continue to Glacier. Her safety is paramount.
We turn back. We will help save her clan.

objectives.description: Continue through Glacier's windswept outer pass. Yumi walks in heartbroken silence.

Glacier Outer Territory — Snowy Pass

Takashi's voice is nearly lost beneath the wind. "We chose safety. It was the order. But what price does that safety carry? A princess without a people. I pray Lord Kazuki understands."
Reach Glacier Village's grand ice-and-stone entrance.

Glacier Village Main Entrance

Takashi turns to you with relief and profound sorrow. Yumi stands beside him, distant and silent.

"We fulfilled the mission. She is safe. You have done your duty, shinobi. But the weight of this silence echoes with the cries we left behind. This is safety—but is it salvation? I do not know."
Duty ending: Princess Yumi reaches Glacier alive, but the fate of her people remains uncertain.
objectives.successDescription: You secured the Sakura Bloom bloodline through stern obligation, though the cries left behind will follow you.

objectives.description: Turn back toward Sakura territory. In the narrow gorge, movement above signals an ambush.

Ambush Site — Narrow Gorge

A chilling laugh descends from the ice walls. Lord Genzo drops into the gorge with three elite guards.

"Well, well. The little blossom princess running back to her rotting roots—and foolish shinobi leading her to her doom. That pin will be mine. Then your clan will finally disappear."

Ambush Site — Narrow Gorge

The beacon ignites. A thin spear of blue chakra climbs into the storm.

Genzo laughs. "A tiny flare in this vastness? Help will arrive in time to bury you. Finish them!"
The three Iron Claw Elite Guards attack in a coordinated first wave. Break their formation and protect Yumi.
objectives.drawDescription: The frozen gorge swallows both formations in a bitter stalemate.
objectives.failDescription: The elite formation overwhelms your defense and closes upon Yumi.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the gorge while the Iron Claw closes on Yumi.

objectives.description: With his guards broken, Lord Genzo enters the battle himself. Defeat the Iron Claw leader.
objectives.drawDescription: Genzo falls to one knee, but so do you; neither side can claim victory.
objectives.failDescription: Genzo's earth and wind techniques crush the last line protecting Yumi.
objectives.fleeDescription: You flee the gorge, leaving Sakura's last hope behind.

objectives.description:
Ambush Site — Narrow Gorge

Genzo's weapon falls into the snow. Yumi rushes to Takashi, then faces you through tears.

"We did it! We fought for them. Thank you, shinobi—thank you!"

Takashi leans on his sword. "You chose the harder path—the path of hope. But we must reach the survivors at the ruined outskirts. Your strength has given them a chance."
Press onward to the besieged Sakura Bloom Clan outskirts and rally the survivors.

Sakura Bloom Clan Outskirts — Under Siege

Smoke rolls across burning barricades. Then Princess Yumi steps forward, her mother's pin shining against the ruin.

"My people! Lord Genzo is defeated! We will not fall. We will rebuild!"

Takashi raises his sword. "Help is on the way! We fight for the Princess! We fight for the Sakura Bloom Clan!"

The exhausted survivors rise. Despair becomes defiance.
Hope ending: Genzo is defeated and Princess Yumi transforms the survivors' despair into defiance.
objectives.successDescription: You led Yumi home, shattered the Iron Claw command, and ignited a flame of hope among the Sakura Bloom survivors.
