data.name: Ghost Ship: Pirate King(Hunt)
data.description: Board the Ghost Ship and defeat the Pirate King for a chance at finding buried treasure.

objectives.description: The ghost ship crosses the moon trailing green fire, and the sea goes quiet beneath it. Tonight it anchors close enough to board. Choose your way in.

nextObjectiveId.text: Hail the ship and ask for parley

objectives.description: The Ghostly Bosun waits at the top of the gangplank with the deck watch, powder crates stacked at the rail behind him. He does not ask your business.
Break the deck watch: the Ghostly Bosun and his powder stores.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The cold water takes you and the ship waits, patient as the tide. Board again.
Climb the anchor chain hand over hand before the watch turns. Gather your footing on the wet iron links.
You slip through the hull breach into the bilge, ankle-deep in black water. Something vast unfolds from the weed-wrapped timbers: the Ghostly Bilge Horror.
The Ghostly Bilge Horror rises from the black water.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Horror drags you under the black water and feeds you back out the breach. Climb again.

A tall figure of pale lantern light salutes from the rail: the Ghostly Herald. 'Answer true and walk aboard oathbound. Answer false and answer my blade. What does every sailor keep that the sea always takes?'
'True.' The Herald steps aside and the crew parts before you, all the way to the helm. 'You walk aboard oathbound. The King will know.'
'False.' The Herald draws a slender dueling blade and salutes. 'Then the duel is your answer.'
The Ghostly Herald salutes and begins the duel.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Herald's blade finds you three times and he lets the sea take you, unimpressed. Hail the ship again.
The deck stretches impossibly wide under tattered black sails. Three ways forward: the chart-lit captain's quarters, the stairs down to the gold-breathing hold, or the long walk to the helm.
The Ghostly Navigator looks up from charts of impossible seas, ink swirling off his hands like living shadow. The coded map you need hangs at his belt.
The Ghostly Navigator redraws the room around you.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: Ink and shadow blind you, and you wake back on the deck. The quarters wait.
You cut the coded map free. Landmarks you know, drawn wrong on purpose, and a riddle inked along the margin. The dig site is out there under the moon.
Drifts of gold coin rise taller than a man. The Ghostly Quartermaster steps between you and the crates, coin-weighted maul on his shoulder, ledger chained to his belt. 'Nothing leaves unaccounted.'
The Ghostly Quartermaster hefts the coin-weight maul.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The maul writes you into the ledger and the hold spits you out. Descend again.
The King's retinue holds the helm: two Ghostly Bosuns stand side by side before a crowned throne of ship timber, mirror-perfect down to the knots in their lashes.
The retinue bars the last steps to the throne.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The retinue holds and the helm stays the King's. Walk it again.
Even the oathbound walk through the retinue. Two Ghostly Bosuns bar the last steps to the throne, and neither bows.
The retinue bars the way, oath or no oath.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The retinue holds, oath or no oath. Walk it again.
The margin riddle reads: 'Where the cliff drinks and the stone watches, dig beneath the watcher's shadow.' Three coves lie under the moon.

nextObjectiveId.text: The cove beneath the stone shrine
The cove with the split cliff
The open beach past the reef

objectives.description: You dig until your arms burn. Rusted cutlasses, crab shells, no chest. The watcher's shadow falls elsewhere.
Sand and reef and nothing buried but a dead man's anchor. Read the riddle again.
Dig beneath the stone watcher's shadow before the tide turns.
Your shovel strikes iron, and the beach itself stands up. The Ghostly Guardian erupts from the sand, shell and reef spike crouched around your prize.
The Ghostly Guardian erupts from the sand.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Guardian buries you to the neck and settles back over the chest. The dig site remains.
The Guardian collapses into wet sand and the chest beneath is iron-bound and heavy with promise. X marks the spot.
You read the dead man's map true and took the treasure from the sand itself.
The hold is yours. Crates you can carry sit in the open. Behind them, a black iron vault hums with something worse. Fortune favors the brave.

nextObjectiveId.text: Grab what you can carry and go

objectives.description: You shoulder a crate and make for the gangplank. The Ghostly Bosun stands at the rail one last time, hook in hand.
The Bosun bars the gangplank one last time.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The Bosun hooks you back aboard by the collar. The rail is right there.
You spill onto the beach with your crate as the ship slides back into the dark. A modest haul, and your neck intact.
Not every fortune is worth the vault that guards it. You took the sure thing.
The lock breaks and the hold goes cold. The Ghostly First Mate steps out of the vault's dark behind twin gale cleavers, coat snapping in a wind that should not exist below decks.
The Ghostly First Mate steps out of the vault's dark.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The storm folds you in half and the vault seals itself to wait. Crack it again.
The storm dies with him. The vault stands open, and what the King hid from his own crew is yours.
You woke what greed keeps chained and beat it anyway. Fortune favors the brave.
The Pirate King rises from the crowned throne, green fire guttering along his cutlass. 'Bold. The sea remembers bold.'
The Pirate King rises from the crowned throne.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The King breaks you against the wheel and the crew throws you to the sea, laughing. The helm waits.
The King kneels, green fire dying along the blade. 'Take it, then. Three hundred years I gathered it for someone worth losing to.'
You walked the longest deck straight to the throne and took the hoard from the King himself.
The King rises, and the Herald's word arrives before you do. 'Oathbound. Then you get the King the crew remembers.' The green fire around him turns white.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face the King at his full fury

objectives.description: The green fire turns white. The King the crew remembers steps down from the throne.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You are beaten back.

objectives.description: The enraged King breaks you against the wheel, then waits for the sigil to knit you back together. An oathbound duel does not end until one of you yields. He has not.

The white fire dies and the King kneels, laughing through broken teeth. 'Oath kept.' He presses the hoard's key into your hand himself. The best of his treasure was always reserved for the one who earned it.
You answered true, dueled with honor, and broke the King at his strongest. No richer night exists aboard the Ghost Ship.

data.name: The Path of a Shinobi: The Jonin Exam
data.description:
"The Mortal King," Haki begins, his voice echoing in the stillness, "is no mere legend.
He is a celestial being whose presence alone disturbs the balance of our world.
He walks the line between divinity and mortality, wielding powers that can reshape the very fabric of Seichi."

He gestures toward a map spread across the table.
Marked upon it are several locations where traces of the Mortal King's presence have been detected—places where the laws of nature have been twisted, and chaos has ensued.
Wildfire erupts in the Shining Dunes without cause; eternal storms rage in Akikaze's Whirling Valley; ice forms in Hyorin's Frozen Highlands, not of Kuraokami's making, but of something far more sinister.

"Your mission is to track these disturbances," Haki continues, his eyes locking onto each Chunin in turn.
"Investigate the traces left behind by this celestial figure.
Find out what he seeks, and most importantly, prevent him from reaching the Monarch Powers—ancient forces that, if combined with his celestial abilities, could plunge our world into irreversible darkness."

The Chunin exchange glances, their resolve hardening.
Each of them carries the weight of their village on their shoulders, but none falter.
They understand the stakes—failure is not an option.

Haki pauses, allowing the gravity of his words to sink in.
Then, with a final nod, he concludes, "You will face not just the Mortal King, but those who serve him—beings of great power and deception.
Trust in your training, in each other, and in Seichi.
Dismissed."
data.successDescription:
They have won, but the victory is bittersweet.
Haki, once their leader, now lies defeated and broken.
The Monarch Powers remain beyond their reach, but Seichi is safe—for now.

As they make their way back to the surface, the Chunin know that their journey is far from over.
The world may never know of their sacrifice, of the betrayal they faced, or of the celestial judgment that looms over them.
But they carry the lessons of this mission with them, a reminder that even in the darkest moments, honor and duty must guide their path.

And somewhere, far beyond the mortal realm, the Mortal King watches, waiting for the day when the balance of Seichi will be tested once more. The monarch is coming and this fragile peace will be broken.

objectives.description: The closer the team gets to unraveling the mystery, the more formidable their enemies become. The Mortal King’s servants, twisted reflections of celestial beings, emerge from the shadows. They are powerful foes—masters of forgotten jutsus, wielders of ancient weapons, and manipulators of dark chakra. Each battle is a test of not just skill but willpower, as the Chunin are forced to confront the very essence of fear and despair.  Yet, through it all, the Chunin fight on, driven by the knowledge that the fate of Seichi rests on their shoulders. They push their limits, discovering new strengths within themselves and forging unbreakable bonds with one another.
The wind spirit Yasei is here, defeat her and then head to the next location.

objectives.description: The mission to uncover the Mortal King’s servants brings the Chunin to the Whirling Valley—a place as unforgiving as it is mysterious. Nestled between the Tornado Valley and Windswept Grasslands, the valley is infamous for its brutal winds and treacherous terrain. Yet, this harsh environment has become a refuge for those who serve the celestial figure, hiding in the chaos of the valley's ever-changing landscape.  The Chunin, tasked with tracking down these elusive servants, quickly realize that the Whirling Valley is unlike any other place they have encountered. The wind here is not just a force of nature; it is a barrier, a guardian of secrets. The valley’s relentless gales twist and turn, obscuring paths and covering tracks, making it nearly impossible to follow any conventional trail. The wind howls like a living creature, and the air is thick with the scent of danger.  Every step through the valley is a battle. The ground beneath their feet is unstable, shifting with the constant pressure of the wind. Loose rocks and sharp ridges make the terrain hazardous, and even the most skilled Shinobi must move with caution. But it is not just the physical dangers that test them—there is an eerie presence in the valley, a sense that they are being watched, hunted even, by forces unseen.

objectives.successDescription: As the servant falls, defeated, the winds begin to calm, and the valley grows quiet. The Chunin stand amidst the ruins of their battle, exhausted but victorious. They have uncovered a crucial piece of the puzzle, a revelation that will bring them one step closer to the Mortal King himself. The Map Points to the Frozen Highlands

objectives.description:
The journey of the Chunin has led them to an ancient ruin in the ironwood forest, a place forgotten by time and untouched by the living. The air is heavy with the presence of the celestial being known as the Mortal King. The ground beneath them hums with energy as they enter the final chamber, a vast space carved from stone and adorned with cryptic symbols that seem to shift and change with every glance. In the center of the chamber, a massive altar looms, pulsing with an otherworldly light. The Chunin can feel the power radiating from it, a force so overwhelming that it threatens to tear apart the fabric of reality itself. They know that this is where the Mortal King plans to unlock the Monarch Powers—a moment that could change the fate of Seichi forever. But as they prepare to confront the celestial being, something feels off. Haki, their enigmatic leader, stands before the altar, his back turned to them. His figure, usually so composed and commanding, now seems shrouded in a dark, almost malevolent energy. One of the Chunin speaks up, their voice laced with concern. "Haki, what are you doing? We need to stop the Mortal King!" Haki doesn't turn to face them. Instead, his voice echoes through the chamber, cold and detached.
"Stop him? No, I have no intention of stopping him. In fact, I have no intention of letting any of you leave this place alive."

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: "You... fools,"Haki spits, his voice weak. "You could have had everything. Now you've doomed us all. But before he can say more, the Mortal King finally speaks. His voice is deep and resonant, echoing through the chamber like the tolling of a bell. "Doomed? No. You misunderstand, Haki." The Chunin turn to face the celestial figure, who has remained silent until now. The Mortal King gazes at them with eyes that seem to hold the weight of countless stars. There is no anger in his expression, no malice—only a calm, almost serene acceptance of what has transpired. "I did not intervene because this was never about power," the Mortal King continues. "It was about judgment. You sought to claim what was not yours, Haki, and in doing so, you revealed the darkness within your heart. But these Chunin—despite their trials, despite your betrayal—chose to act with honor. The Mortal King raises a hand, and for a moment, it seems as though he might unleash his celestial power upon them all. But instead, he simply turns away, his form beginning to dissolve into light. "The balance of Seichi will be restored," he says, his voice fading. "But remember this, mortals: true power lies not in strength or ambition, but in understanding the limits of one's own desires. I will be watching."

data.name: The Shattered Sakura: Part 2 - Whispers of Home
data.description: Princess Yumi's whispered words revealed her longing for a lost cherry blossom pin: a memento of her mother and her shattered home. Against the original mission parameters, you and Takashi return to the Sakura Bloom ruins, where desperate survivors and Iron Claw scavengers haunt the echoes of war.
data.successDescription: You recovered Princess Yumi's Mother's Cherry Blossom Pin from the ruins and defeated the Iron Claw scavengers. Yumi's first fragile smile restored a small piece of hope, even as the escort toward Glacier—and harder choices—continues.

objectives.description:
You've made the decision to return for the pin. Takashi, though uneasy, nods in grim understanding. Princess Yumi looks up with a fleeting spark in her eyes.

Takashi lowers his voice. “The pin... a fragment of her mother's warmth. Expediency is one thing, but a broken spirit is another. The ruins of our home—Sector 87, coordinates 8,8—will be crawling with scavengers, perhaps even the Iron Claw. We must be swift. Princess, stay close. We go for your mother's memory.”
You begin the journey back to the Sakura Bloom Clan's ruined settlement. The air grows heavy with a sense of loss.

The devastation is worse than imagined. Buildings have become charcoal, the ground is scarred, and fresh tracks cross the snow.

Takashi clenches his fist. “Our home... This is what ‘victory’ looks like for the powerful. Desolation for the small. Yumi's mother often left sacred offerings at the Clan Shrine—Sector 88, coordinates 12,12. That's where we begin.”
You escort Yumi and Takashi through the ruins toward the damaged Clan Shrine. Only the wind disturbs the silence.

A gaunt survivor claws through the overturned offering box. She recoils when she sees you.

Ryoko's voice trembles. “Please! Don't hurt me! I'm just looking for food... or anything. They took everything. The Iron Claw come and go, taking what's left.” Her eyes find Yumi. “Princess Yumi? You're... alive?”

nextObjectiveId.text: Takashi comforts Ryoko. “We need the Princess's pin. Did you see it?”
Focus on the mission. “Have you seen a small cherry blossom pin?”

objectives.description: Tears gather in Ryoko's hollow eyes. “The pin... no. But the Iron Claw scavengers went through the barracks—Sector 89, coordinates 5,10. They take anything shiny. Sometimes they fight among themselves over trinkets. It may be there... if they haven't destroyed it.”
You leave Ryoko and advance toward the ruined barracks, her warning about Iron Claw scavengers ringing in your ears.

Broken weapons and empty crates cover the barracks floor. Rough voices carry from the next room. “This scrap isn't worth much. But the other fellow had a fancy pin—said it glowed. Wonder where he stashed it.”

Takashi whispers fiercely, “Iron Claw. They're still here, and they have the pin. Princess, stay behind me.”
Defeat all three Iron Claw Scavengers and recover Mother's Cherry Blossom Pin.
objectives.drawDescription: Both sides recoil from the ruined chamber, bloodied but unbroken.
objectives.failDescription: The scavengers overwhelm you. Takashi drags you behind a collapsed wall before the killing blow lands.
objectives.fleeDescription: You retreat into the barracks rubble before the Iron Claw can surround Yumi.
objectives.successDescription: The final scavenger falls. A faint, warm sakura light shines beneath his torn armor.

objectives.description: Takashi binds your wounds while Yumi watches from the shadows. Regroup, breathe, and confront the scavengers again.
You retrieve Mother's Cherry Blossom Pin. Polished wood and silver form a blooming sakura, glowing with faint protective chakra.
objectives.successDescription: The pin's warmth steadies in your hand as though recognizing Yumi nearby.

objectives.description:
Takashi cleans the pin with trembling hands and places it in Yumi's palm. A tiny, fragile smile touches her lips.

“Mama...” Yumi whispers, clutching the pin. “It's warm.” She looks at you with genuine gratitude.

Takashi clears his throat. “She remembers. Thank you, shinobi. This is more than a pin. It's a flicker of hope. But the Iron Claw will return. Dawn approaches; we head toward Glacier as planned.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Her smile is worth it. Let's go.

objectives.description: You leave the devastated ruins behind. Dawn filters through the forest, and Yumi walks with the warm pin held close.

The pale dawn illuminates the forest path. Takashi looks at you with profound gratitude. “You risked much for her small hope. This is what true protection means. We continue toward the safety Lord Kazuki insists upon. But her words, her smile... they stir something in me. For now, we follow orders. This journey is far from over.”

Next: The Shattered Sakura: Part 3 - A Crossroads of Duty. Having recovered Yumi's pin, the journey to Glacier continues—but Iron Claw aggression and Yumi's awakening hope will soon force a choice between duty and a shattered home.

Plant your seeds to complete the objective.

Great job watering those plants. Make sure to water them periodically. Now, let's add some fertilizers. Fertilizers also reduce your farming time and make your plants grow big and strong.

Take these fertilizers, go to your home, select a plot, and select Fertilize.

Harvesting is the process of reaping your crops after all the hard work you put into caring for them, including watering and fertilizing.
Once you harvest your plants, you can use seed extraction to get more seeds or sell them for Farm coins, which can be used to purchase other seeds and plots and to buy more fertilizers.

data.name: The Silken Thread Unravels
data.description: The Crystal Weaver has been defeated and peace is restored to  Yukigumo Village. Or so you think. A message comes for you in the middle of the night, a taunt and an invitation both. Will you answer the call?
data.successDescription: You have won after a long struggle. You’ve fought for peace and saved the lives of Yukigumo village’s citizens. But still… a haunting chill lingers in the wind.

objectives.description: A letter has arrived for you from Yukigumo Village. Meanwhile, the disappearances have escalated since then. Head out at once and investigate what’s happening.

The letter is heavy, made with fine parchment. It shines in the light with silvery lines that look somewhat like snowflakes. Breaking the seal, you read the contents of the letter.  "You have fought bravely, and our people are free thanks to you. Come—join us for a feast in your honor, so we may celebrate the peace you’ve given us."
You return to the snowbound village where the cult was last seen. Following the letter’s directions, you arrive at a grand hall ablaze with lantern light.

Inside, a long banquet table stretches across the chamber, filled with smiling guests. Whispers ripple among them—you hear that each has received a letter, just like yours. Tonight is meant to celebrate peace, and you are the guest of honor. Do you take your place at the table or mingle with the guests more?

You wander among the guests, exchanging pleasantries while watching the food being served. From your vantage, you notice something strange: the servers bear pale, glimmering tattoos on their wrists. In the lanternlight, you can’t tell whether they’re meant to be snowflakes… or spiderwebs.  Before you can decide to approach one, a bell is chimed clearly indicating that the banquet has begun.

You lose yourself in the celebration. The tables are heaped with roasted wildfowl, platters of steaming vegetables, tender cuts of meat stacked high, and fruit so ripe it glistens. Goblets of spiced wine and mulled rum never seem to empty.   But as the night wears on, your body grows heavy. Your eyes droop, the warmth fades, and a biting chill seeps in.

nextObjectiveId.text: When… did it get so cold?

objectives.description: You awake in a cellar, your wrists bound tightly in rope. Around you, the other guests lie unconscious, trapped in the same fate. On the floor nearby lies a shard of glass. In one corner, a jagged piece of old wood juts from the stone walls. In the distance, you hear footsteps fast approaching. How do you escape?

You stealthily try to follow one of the servers as he makes his way towards the back. He turns towards a hallway and as you follow, you accidentally step on a trip wire.  He spins around with eerie grace and you hear an inhuman hiss
Your opponent flies towards you in a flurry of blades.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: The fight has drawn the attention of another server. The battle has not yet ended. It has only begun
Reality bends around you as the battle kicks up.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: As the battle ends, the last server heads towards you to join the fight

objectives.description: You cannot abandon the other guests—not while danger lingers. Securing the cellar, you follow the only corridor deeper into the earth.
It crumbles to dust. Footsteps approach. Robed figures enter. A sharp blow to the back of your head sends you into darkness.
You free yourself just in time to face your opponents. You recognize them as the servers from the banquet by the shimmery tattoos of spiderwebs that cover their skin.

Although clumsy, you note that the new Crystal Weaver has only grown stronger.

data.name: Ren of Wake Island III: The Mask Beyond Borders
data.description: Ren enters the border crisis as a Jonin and Global ANBU candidate, carrying the lessons you gave them into a war that may begin with one wrong truth.
data.successDescription: Ren chooses the face beneath the Tidebreaker Mask and steps into their future.

objectives.description: Ren is no longer nervous. They are calm, capable, and starting to act before asking. Wake Island assigns you to stop a border war.
Travel to the neutral sandbar where both allied villages claim the other side drew first blood.
Survivors are wounded, angry, and lying. Ren waits for the method you choose when war is one bad answer away.

nextObjectiveId.text: Plant false evidence to delay retaliation.

objectives.description: Ren kneels beside the tracks. 'Patience can prevent war before anyone praises it.'
Ren listens to a survivor break. 'Pressure creates answers. Whether they are true is the next problem.'
Ren pockets the forged marker. 'A lie can buy time for the truth to arrive.'
Ren does not look away from the bodies. 'Sacrifice can reveal truth. That does not make it clean.'
Move to the prisoner skiff where a flagless provocateur waits under guard.
The prisoner's escorts attack to erase the interrogation. Keep the provocateur alive long enough to speak.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The skiff fight breaks formation. Return to the prisoner route and secure the witness.
The provocateur tells Ren that peace is just violence wearing clean clothes.

nextObjectiveId.text: Refuse torture and seek another way.

objectives.description: Ren's hands unclench. 'Restraint under pressure is not weakness. It is command.'
Ren asks three quiet questions. The prisoner answers the fourth before it is spoken.
Ren watches without flinching. 'Cruelty can be acceptable if the alternative is worse. That is what you showed me.'
Ren studies the prisoner's fear. 'Enemies can be resources with a pulse.'
Return to Wake Island Summit Hall before the ambassadors arrive armed.
The summit begins with incomplete truth. Assassins prepare to kill both ambassadors and leave the war no witness.

nextObjectiveId.text: Reveal truth and trust the ambassadors.
Control the summit from the shadows.

objectives.description: Ren looks almost young again. 'Trust is risky, but maybe peace cannot breathe without it.'
Ren's voice is calm. 'Peace can be engineered if no one sees the hands.'
Ren wipes their blade. 'Dead enemies cannot complicate the story.'
Ren steps ahead of you. 'I already know what you would do. Now I need to know what I will do.'
Hold the summit floor against the assassins before the ambassadors turn on each other.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends without a clear victor.
objectives.failDescription: Ren stumbles backward as the tide turns against you.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren away before the fight can finish.
objectives.successDescription: Ren exhales and studies what your choice made possible.

objectives.description: The summit fractures. Return to the hall approach and stop the assassination cleanly.
Follow Ren to the chamber where the Tidebreaker Mask waits.
The enemy leader offers Ren a place beyond Wake Island. Ren turns to you for the final face beneath the mask.

nextObjectiveId.text: Gray Tide: peace works in shadow.

objectives.description: Ren becomes the White Tide. 'A shinobi's hands will never stay clean. That does not mean their heart has to rot.'
Ren becomes the Black Tide. 'You taught me results matter more than excuses. I stopped pretending there were lines.'
Ren becomes the Gray Tide. 'Heroes save people where others can see. Shinobi save them where no one asks the cost.'
Ren becomes the Redeemed Blade. 'Someone should have told me power was not purpose. So I will tell them.'
Ren's Tidebreaker candidacy ends with a mask, a path, and the shape of every lesson you let them keep.

data.description:
Freedom State doesn’t sleep.



By dawn, the lanterns still burn green, their glow staining the sky. The once-lively market streets are quiet — masks abandoned, music silenced, and offerings left to smolder in their trays.



Before noon, messengers arrive with grim news: the corruption has spread. Every village that lit Veilnight lanterns reports the same eerie transformation — their flames turned green, their nights filled with distant laughter.



This isn’t a local disturbance.


It’s an echo moving through all of Seichi.



“If his influence is riding the light,” someone says, “then every lantern we kindled last night opened a door.”



Your Momo follows silently now, her energy unstable, the green flicker still buried behind her eyes. She flinches at each whisper of laughter that drifts in on the wind.
data.successDescription:
Each victory quiets the laughter only for a moment. Every village’s lantern burns green again before dimming — sending a pulse of light back toward Freedom State.
When the final echo fades, it’s clear where all of this leads.
The heart of the disturbance has never left the Lantern of Balance.
Grimjack (distant): “The farther you run, the closer you are.”

By nightfall, the lantern in Freedom State blazes brighter than ever, green fire clawing at the sky.

objectives.description: Trace Grimjack’s spreading influence across Seichi. The corruption manifests differently in each village, warping its natural balance.
When the storms grow louder and the air crackles with unseen tension, follow the wetlands where lightning kisses the earth and secrets wait beneath the fog.

data.name: The Wyrmspire Nest
data.description: Livestock and travelers have vanished along the mountain roads. Scouts traced wing-shadows to an obsidian spire riddled with nesting tunnels. Destroy the brood before the clutch hatches and the skies belong to dragons.

objectives.description: A scout presses a scorched satchel into your hands, all that remains of the last patrol. She points to the obsidian spire on the horizon: the wing-shadows nest there. Track the first wyvern along the foothill trail.

The caldera opens to the sky. Wyrmspire Elder Vulkar uncoils from the nest heart, scales older than the mountain, breath like a forge. It knows what you did below.

data.name: The Silent Bells of Winter-Hard -
data.description: A supernatural winter has descended without wind or warning. Snowmen appear where none were built, and silent Moonprowlers circle the settlements. At the center of this anomaly is a massive, sentient snowman—Ava the Snow Terror. She is invulnerable to standard steel. You must hunt her elven lieutenants, Axel and Dagger, and the prowling beasts to gather the materials needed to forge the Candy Cane Blade, the only weapon capable of cracking her frost-core.
data.successDescription: The Candy Cane Blade strikes true, shattering Ava's frost-core. The unnatural winter breaks instantly. The snowmen collapse into harmless drifts, the elves vanish, and the haunting bells finally fall silent. The village is safe, though the memory of the watching snow will linger forever.

objectives.description: The snow fell without warning. No storm. No wind. Just... silence. And now She is here. Ava, the Snow Terror. She stands taller than the roofs, watching. We cannot hurt her; she rebuilds herself instantly. But the legends speak of a weapon—the Candy Cane Blade. Only it can crack her core. You must gather the parts and forge it yourself. Seek the beasts at the treeline first
Head to the Moonlit Treeline where the Moonprowlers are circling the village.

data.name: One White Ear
data.description: Elder Yukino's cat has gone over the fence into the snow again. Search the treeline for Mochi and bring her home.
data.successDescription: Good Job, you have found the cat. Now that I think about it, this is the fourth time this week.

objectives.description:
Elder Yukino waits at her gate with a scarf twisted between her hands, snow settling on her shoulders.

"Mochi is gone again. Grey, one white ear, a temper like a storm cloud.
She went over the fence at first light and the treeline swallowed her. My knees are not what they were, shinobi."

nextObjectiveId.text: A cat hunt. You owe me tea for this.

objectives.description: Follow the paw prints in the fresh snow to the treeline east of the village.

The treeline is quiet enough to hear your own breath. Somewhere in the white a thin mewling starts, stops, and starts again.

The sound bends around the trunks. It could be coming from anywhere.

nextObjectiveId.text: Search the drifts along the fence line.
Follow the cart tracks up the open path.
Listen again, then head for the old pine.

objectives.description:
Snow, a startled squirrel, and cold working its way into your boots. Nothing else.

The mewling starts again somewhere behind you. Wrong place. Try again.

Paw prints run straight to the base of the old pine and stop at a hollow worn into the roots. Something inside shifts its weight.

Two eyes catch the light in the dark, daring you to try something.

nextObjectiveId.text: Reach in slowly and speak softly.
Offer the dried fish from your ration pack.

objectives.description:
She takes her time deciding, then comes out on her own terms: one bite on principle for the hand, a long look for the fish, and a decision made in her favour either way.

She climbs your sleeve and arranges herself across your shoulders as though this was her plan from the start.
Carry Mochi back through the snow to Elder Yukino's gate.

The elder scoops her up and the storm cloud dissolves into shameless purring.

"You wretch. You had me sick with worry."
She presses your payment into your hand with a rice ball still warm from the stove, for the road, and for the bite she suspects you earned.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the payment and the rice ball.

data.name: [Path of Crimson] [Part I: The Sunset Road]
data.description:
You step into the Administration Building at Wake Island. The air is heavy with the scent of burning incense, mingling with faint traces of ash. Dusk is waiting by the window, his glowing eyes fixed on the horizon. His golden scarf billows gently, though there’s no wind.

"Ah, there you are. I’ve been waiting. The Sunset Road is burning—quite literally. Caravans have been destroyed, cargo vanished, and the culprits remain in the shadows.”

“This isn’t random. It reeks of the Black Maw. They don’t simply attack—they calculate, they take, and they leave nothing but ash in their wake.”

“I need you to investigate. Follow the trail. Find out what they’re after. And if you run into resistance...”

Dusk smirks, his fiery scarf shifting with the breeze.

“Well, let’s just say they won’t be calculating much after you’re done.”

“Start at the caravan site. You’ll find it near Sector 338. And remember—anything you find may burn, but it won’t destroy the truth.”
data.successDescription: See you in seven days. ~ DUSK ~

data.name: The Borrowed Awakening: The Reworked Pair
data.description: The archive opens two reworked vessels this weekend, and each comes with the gear it needs. You may take exactly one. A broken seal is final, and the vessel you leave stays shut.
data.successDescription: You carry a reworked echo, and the tools that make it worth carrying. It was never yours to keep.

objectives.description: Two vessels on the counter, and the archivist sets a small locked case beside each one. "These two were reworked," she says. "They do not come alone. Take the vessel and you take what it needs to be worth taking." She steps back. "One of them. Lift both, weigh both, put them back as often as you like. A broken seal is a closed archive."

nextObjectiveId.text: Take up the pale blue vessel (Blue Edge Eyes)
Take up the dark red vessel (Blood-Enthralled Eyes)

objectives.description: Cold through the wrapping, and the light inside moves like something watching. This is the Blue Edge line: control and burst, eight jutsu at their ceiling, and the two weapons that answer only to it. They come with the seal. Break this and you carry it until the doors close. The other vessel stays shut for you.

nextObjectiveId.text: Break the seal. Blue Edge Eyes is my choice
Put it back and weigh the other

objectives.description: Warm. Warmer than your hand, and it keeps getting warmer. This is the Blood-Enthralled line: burst healing and sustained damage, eight jutsu at their ceiling, and the two keystones that carry its paths. They come with the seal. Break this and you carry it until the doors close. The other vessel stays shut for you.

nextObjectiveId.text: Break the seal. Blood-Enthralled Eyes is my choice
Put it back and weigh the other

objectives.successDescription: The seal splits along a line you did not see until it opened. Cold light climbs the inside of your skull, and for a moment every edge in the room separates from the thing it casts. The archivist marks her ledger once and closes it. Blue Edge Eyes is yours, weapons and all, until the doors close.

Warmth spreads from the wrist inward, unhurried, the way a debt spreads. Somewhere under your own heartbeat a second one starts, half a step behind and patient. The archivist marks her ledger once and closes it. Blood-Enthralled Eyes is yours, keystones and all, until the doors close.

objectives.description: You set the vessel back on the counter, still sealed, and the case beside it stays shut. The archivist does not look up. "Nothing is spent," she says. "Nothing is spent until it breaks."

data.name: Story: The Ember Ledger
data.description: A Chunin field-command mission investigating the stolen Ember Ledger, a classified Wake Island record that exposes candidate vulnerabilities and forces Ren to decide what kind of shinobi leadership means.
data.successDescription: The Ember Ledger is recovered, Kaito Vey is defeated, and Ren leaves the mission changed by the player's command choices.

objectives.description: Captain Iori stands beside a sealed briefing table. The air smells of ink, rain, and old paper. Ren is already there, trying very hard not to look proud. Captain Iori: "You are Chunin now. That means the village no longer asks whether you can survive danger. We ask whether others can survive under your command." Ren: "I won't slow you down. I swear it." Captain Iori: "That is exactly the wrong promise, Ren. A subordinate who only thinks about not being a burden becomes one." Ren: "Then... what should I promise?" Captain Iori: "To listen. To report. To stay alive." The captain turns to the player. Captain Iori: "The Ember Ledger was stolen last night. It contains classified evaluations from the fast-track program. Combat potential, psychological vulnerabilities, projected loyalty risks. If exposed, it would damage command trust across every village that cooperates with Wake Island." Ren's smile fades. Ren: "Psychological vulnerabilities?" Captain Iori: "Everyone in the program has a file."
The player chooses how to respond to Ren's discomfort.
Reassure Ren "You are more than whatever they wrote." Ren exhales, but their eyes stay fixed on the sealed table. Ren: "Then I'll prove it by how I act, not by what they predicted."
Harden Ren "If they found weaknesses, fix them." Ren nods sharply. Ren: "Right. Weakness only matters if you leave it alive."
Deflect the issue "Files are tools. Don't take it personally." Ren looks down. Ren: "So I'm a tool being measured by other tools."
Stay mission-focused "We recover the ledger first. Feelings later." Ren straightens immediately. Ren: "Yes. Mission first."

Captain Iori: "The thief left no blood, no broken lock, and no chakra burn. That means either they had credentials, or someone inside helped them." She places three evidence slips on the table. 1. A burned paper charm 2. A red thread 3. A false transfer order stamped with an old instructor seal Captain Iori: "You will start at the archive. Take Ren. Watch how they respond. This mission is an investigation, not a hunt."

Archivist Sena waits under the archive awning. Her hands are wrapped around a cup of tea she has not touched. Sena: "I told the captain everything." Ren whispers. Ren: "No one says that unless they left something out."
The player chooses how to question Sena.

Sena: "The person wore an old instructor cloak. Gray trim. Burn marks along the sleeve." Ren turns to the player. Ren: "That means former staff." Sena: "There was a name once. Kaito Vey. He trained candidates before the current program existed."
The player searches the archive. Found evidence: - Broken wax seal - Scorched index card - Partial list of copied files - Ren's candidate number circled in red Ren goes silent.
Ren: "That number is mine." They try to laugh, but it comes out thin. Ren: "Maybe they just picked names at random." Ren looks at the player, hoping the player will agree.
Ren looks to the player, hoping for an answer about why their candidate number was circled.
Be honest but kind "It probably was not random. But that does not mean they understand you." Ren: "Then I need to understand them first."
Encourage anger "They targeted you. Remember that." Ren: "I will." Their voice becomes colder.
Hide concern "We do not know enough yet." Ren: "You know more than you're saying."
Redirect to duty "Emotions can wait. Evidence cannot." Ren: "Yes, commander." The title sounds heavier than before.
On the roof, the player finds ash pressed into the shape of a handprint. Ren kneels beside it. Ren: "This was left on purpose."
A masked scout rises from behind the water tower. Mura: "Still using children to chase ghosts?" Ren reaches for their weapon. Ren: "I'm not a child." Mura: "That's what they taught me to say too."
Battle against Mura, Ember Hand Scout. Fail condition routes to recovery objective.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends unresolved beneath the rain and ash.
objectives.failDescription: The Ember Hand overwhelms the field. Regroup, study the pressure, and try again.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren back before the fight can decide the mission without you.

objectives.description: If defeated, the player and Ren fall back. Ren: "We lost because I moved too early." Ren clenches their fists. Ren: "Tell me what to fix."
After victory, Mura is disarmed. Mura: "Go on, then. Prove you're what they made you."

If spared or questioned, Mura gives a clue. Mura: "Kaito doesn't want the ledger sold. He wants it read aloud. Every name. Every weakness. Every lie Wake Island wrapped in a uniform." Ren steps forward. Ren: "And my file?" Mura: "He circled the names he thought were already breaking."
Rain begins to fall. Ren: "Commander... when someone writes down the worst parts of you, are they recording the truth, or creating it?"

Captain Iori: "Kaito Vey was dismissed after refusing to submit candidate mortality projections. He believed the program was becoming too aggressive." Ren folds their arms. Ren: "Was he wrong?" The room quiets.
Choose how to respond.

The player investigates the training yard where Kaito once taught. Found evidence: - Training posts burned from inside - Children's practice tags - Old lesson board: "A shinobi who cannot choose will be chosen for."
Ren reads the board. Ren: "I hate that." A pause. Ren: "I also understand it."

A lingering genjutsu seal activates. Kaito's recorded voice plays. Kaito's Echo: "Students, command will praise your potential until your usefulness expires. Learn the difference between being valued and being spent." Ren flinches.
Ren waits to see how the player answers Kaito's recorded bitterness.
Reject Kaito's bitterness "He is using pain to sound wise." Ren: "Pain can still tell the truth."
Admit he has a point "Sometimes systems do spend people." Ren looks relieved that the player said it first.
Tell Ren not to listen "Enemy propaganda. Ignore it." Ren: "I can ignore the voice. Not the feeling."
Ask Ren what they think "What did you hear?" Ren: "Someone who loved his students and started hating everyone else."
The player finds a hidden compartment containing old casualty projections. Ren sees names blacked out. Ren: "These were Genin?"
Ren: "Commander, if a mission has a seventy percent chance of killing a Genin, is it wrong to send them?" This is not theoretical to Ren.
Ren asks whether children should ever be sent into a war zone.
Protective answer "Yes, unless there is absolutely no other way." Ren: "Then a leader's job is to find another way."
Harsh answer "War does not care about age." Ren: "Then I need to stop caring before war uses that against me."
Conditional answer "It depends on what is at stake." Ren: "That answer scares me because it sounds useful."
Reflect question back "What would you do?" Ren: "I'd go myself first. But maybe that is selfish too."
A ledger seal erupts into a defensive construct. Ren: "Archive guardian! It's made from copied chakra signatures!"
Battle against Ledger-Bound Construct.
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends unresolved beneath the rain and ash.
objectives.failDescription: The Ember Hand overwhelms the field. Regroup, study the pressure, and try again.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren back before the fight can decide the mission without you.

objectives.description: If defeated, the player falls back. Ren: "It copied our timing. We need to change rhythm, not just hit harder."
The construct leaves behind a coded ember slip. Decoded phrase: "Public reading at the drowned bell."
Ren: "The drowned bell... that's the abandoned signal tower near the lower docks." They hesitate. Ren: "If Kaito wants people to hear the ledger, he's not hiding anymore."
Choose how to respond.

Ren walks beside the player in the rain. Ren: "When I was younger, I thought Chunin were just Genin who got stronger. Now I think Chunin are people who have to make decisions before anyone forgives them."
The lower docks are crowded. Workers whisper about a public confession. Someone has painted a red hand across the old signal tower.
Dock Merchant: "You shinobi lost something, didn't you? That's why everyone looks scared." Ren steps forward. Ren: "Please stay away from the tower." Dock Merchant: "And miss the truth? No chance."
Choose how to respond.
The player finds explosive tags disguised as announcement papers. Ren pales. Ren: "He wanted a crowd."
The player and Ren begin removing explosive tags.
Ren: "If Kaito really wanted to save students, why risk civilians?" The question lands hard.
Choose how to respond.

The Red Scribe descends from the rafters, mask painted with a smiling mouth. Red Scribe: "The candidate arrives with their handler." Ren stiffens. Ren: "Do not call them that." Red Scribe: "Oh? Then what should I call the one holding your leash?"
Battle against The Red Scribe.

objectives.failDescription: The Ember Hand overwhelms the field. Regroup, study the pressure, and try again.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren back before the fight can decide the mission without you.

objectives.description: If defeated, Ren drags the player behind cover. Ren: "He attacks the mind before the body. Don't answer his questions unless you choose to."

After victory, the Red Scribe laughs through a cracked mask. Red Scribe: "Ren. Candidate temperament: approval-seeking, guilt-responsive, high mimicry index." Ren freezes. Red Scribe: "You become what stands nearest."
The Red Scribe twists Ren's file into an accusation. How does the player answer?
Protect Ren emotionally "Ren is standing nearest to me. Choose your next words carefully." Ren's expression softens.
Demand the full file "Keep talking. What else does it say?" Ren looks wounded but listens.
Silence the Scribe "Enough." The player ends the interrogation.
Let Ren confront him "Ren. Answer him." Ren steps forward. Ren: "If I become what stands nearest, then I'd better choose carefully."
Found: - Partial copy of Ren's profile - Broadcast seal - Kaito's location: Bell Chamber
Ren grips the copied file. Ren: "Approval-seeking. Guilt-responsive. High mimicry index." They laugh bitterly. Ren: "That sounds more like a weapon description than a person."
Ren grips the copied file and waits for the player's response.
Affirm identity "A file can describe habits. It cannot decide who you become." Ren: "Then I want my choices to be louder than their notes."
Turn it into tactical advice "Now you know what enemies will target." Ren: "Then I remove the target."
Minimize it "Everyone has a file." Ren: "That does not make it less ugly."
Apologize for the system "You should not have found out this way." Ren looks surprised. Ren: "No one ever apologizes for systems. Only mistakes."
Kaito's voice echoes from beyond the door. Kaito Vey: "Come in, Chunin. Bring the child they taught you to command." Ren whispers. Ren: "I am not afraid." But they are.

Kaito stands beside the stolen ledger. Broadcast seals circle the chamber like red fireflies. Kaito: "You came faster than command predicted. Good. That means at least one of you still has instincts." Ren: "You stole our files." Kaito: "I stole proof."
Choose how to respond.

Kaito: "Ren was circled because they are exactly what the program loves. Adaptable. Hungry for approval. Easy to shape. Put them beside a saint, they become noble. Put them beside a butcher, they become efficient." Ren looks at the player. Kaito: "That is not an insult. It is a warning."
Kaito tries to claim Ren's lesson. How does the player answer?
Tell Ren to choose for themselves "Then Ren's first real lesson is choosing who not to become." Ren: "I choose with open eyes."
Claim responsibility for Ren "They are under my command. I decide what they learn." Kaito smiles sadly. Kaito: "And there it is."
Reject the discussion "We are done talking." Ren looks uncertain.
Ask Ren what they want "Ren. Not me. Not him. What do you want?" Ren struggles to answer.
Kaito activates the first broadcast seal. Kaito: "One page. One name. Let the island hear what it creates." The first pages begin to glow.
The player must choose a tactical priority.

The chosen priority plays out. Ren reacts based on the player's decision. If Disable Broadcast: Ren: "You protected everyone's names." If Secure Ledger: Ren: "You went for the source." If Capture Kaito: Ren: "You ended the threat first." If Protect Ren: Ren: "You chose me over the mission?"
Battle against Kaito Vey, phase one.

objectives.description: If defeated, Kaito does not kill the player. Kaito: "Stand up. I am not here to murder Chunin. I am here to make them admit what they serve." Ren helps the player rise. Ren: "He's leaving openings. He wants the argument as much as the fight."

Kaito opens Ren's page. Kaito: "Projected risk: identity diffusion under inconsistent mentorship. Recommended solution: stable authority figure, mission exposure, praise regulation." Ren's face goes pale. Ren: "Praise... regulation?"
Kaito exposes Ren's page. Ren is listening.
Condemn the file language "That is a cruel way to describe a person." Ren: "Thank you."
Focus Ren "He is trying to destabilize you. Breathe." Ren: "Breathing. Listening. Not breaking."
Weaponize the anger "Use it. Show him what they failed to predict." Ren's chakra spikes.
Say nothing Ren reads the page alone. Ren: "So that's what I am to them."
Kaito tears one page free and lets it burn. Kaito: "You can recover the ledger. You cannot unread it."
The tower begins to collapse from unstable seals. Ren points to two routes: - One path leads after Kaito. - One path leads to trapped civilians below.
The chamber begins to collapse as civilians are still nearby. Choose the priority.
Save civilians first Ren follows immediately. Ren: "People before victory. Understood."
Chase Kaito Ren hesitates, then follows. Ren: "If he escapes, more people suffer later."
Split up Ren goes to civilians while player chases Kaito. Ren: "You trust me with lives?"
Order Ren to decide Ren freezes for half a second. Ren: "No. I choose civilians. You choose Kaito. Move!"
If civilians are prioritized, the player pulls workers from the collapsing lower walkway. If Kaito is prioritized, this objective becomes a delayed rescue with more panic.
Civilian Worker: "I thought shinobi only protected secrets." Ren answers before the player can. Ren: "Today we protect people too."
Ren nearly falls while crossing a broken support beam. The player can help, command, or pressure them.
Ren freezes on the collapsing tower spine. How does the player help?
Encourage calmly "Look at me. One step at a time." Ren: "One step. Then another. I can do that."
Command sharply "Move, Ren. Now." Ren moves fast, frightened but effective.
Leap back and carry them Ren is saved, but frustrated. Ren: "I could have done it."
Make them solve it "Find your route. I trust your read." Ren finds a safer angle. Ren: "You really meant that."
The player recovers scattered ledger pages. One page belongs to Mura. It describes Mura as "recoverable only through authority disruption." Ren reads it silently.
Ren: "They wrote him like a broken tool too." A pause. Ren: "Maybe that's why he joined Kaito."
Choose how to respond.
The Red Scribe returns, wounded but laughing. Red Scribe: "One last confession, Ren. Would you like to know what your commander thinks of you?"
Second battle against The Red Scribe.

objectives.description: The Red Scribe is defeated again.
The player reaches the roof access. Kaito is visible above, preparing the final broadcast.
Ren stops. Ren: "Before we go up there... tell me what kind of Chunin I should become."
Ren waits for the player's answer. What kind of Chunin should Ren become?
Guardian Lesson "One who protects people without owning them." Ren: "Then command is not a leash. It's a shelter."
Weapon Lesson "One who ends threats before they multiply." Ren: "Then hesitation is cruelty wearing a gentle face."
Strategist Lesson "One who controls what others are allowed to know." Ren: "Then truth is a blade. You draw it only when needed."
Self-Determination Lesson "One who knows what they refuse to become." Ren closes their eyes. Ren: "Then I need to decide that before someone decides for me."
Kaito's voice rolls down from the roof. Kaito: "Come, Chunin. Bring your answer."

The rain has stopped. The city below glistens under gray morning light. Kaito holds the ledger over an active broadcast seal. Kaito: "One final page. Ren's page. Let the island decide whether the program saves children or sharpens them."
Choose how to respond.

Ren speaks based on accumulated influence. Lantern-leaning Ren: "I was shaped by others. Maybe everyone is. But being shaped is not the same as being owned." Blade-leaning Ren: "You are right about one thing. People like me are dangerous. That is why I will choose my targets carefully." Mask-leaning Ren: "Truth without timing is just another explosion. You taught me that by accident." Ash-leaning Ren: "Maybe all of you are the same. Command. Rebels. Teachers. Handlers. Everyone wants a use for me."
Final battle against Kaito Vey.

objectives.description: If defeated, Kaito disables the broadcast briefly. Kaito: "Again. If they made you leaders, then stand like leaders." Ren wipes blood from their lip. Ren: "He's testing whether we break before our answer does."
Kaito enters his final phase. Kaito: "Show me the future Wake Island deserves."
objectives.drawDescription: The clash ends unresolved beneath the rain and ash.
objectives.failDescription: The Ember Hand overwhelms the field. Regroup, study the pressure, and try again.
objectives.fleeDescription: You pull Ren back before the fight can decide the mission without you.

objectives.description: The ledger falls toward the broadcast seal. Ren dives for it. The player must choose what to secure.
The ledger falls toward the broadcast seal. Ren dives for it. What should the player secure?
Save Ren first The ledger partially broadcasts, but Ren is safe.
Save the ledger first The ledger is secured, but Ren is injured.
Destroy the broadcast seal The ledger is damaged, but no page is released.
Trust Ren with the ledger and stop Kaito Ren catches the ledger alone while the player ends the fight.
Kaito is defeated. Kaito: "So. What did you teach them, Chunin?" Ren answers before the player can.

Ren's response changes by path. Lantern Ren: "They taught me that people are not saved by exposing wounds to a crowd. They are saved when someone stays after seeing them." Blade Ren: "They taught me that mercy without strength is just permission for the next monster." Mask Ren: "They taught me that truth needs a guard. Unguarded truth becomes a weapon." Ash Ren: "They taught me that I need to become something no file, commander, or rebel can predict."
The player decides Kaito's immediate fate.
The player secures what remains of the Ember Ledger.
Ren looks at the ledger. Ren: "I want to burn my page." They do not move. Ren: "But if I burn it because I'm afraid of it, then it still controls me."
Ren looks at the ledger and waits for the player's decision.
Let Ren keep the page sealed "One day, read it when you choose."
Destroy Ren's page "No one owns this version of you."
Captain Iori receives the damaged ledger. Captain Iori: "You recovered it." She looks at Ren. Captain Iori: "And you read part of it." Ren does not look away. Ren: "Yes."
Choose how to respond.

Ren stands outside, watching gulls circle over the wet rooftops. Ren: "I used to think promotion meant people stopped doubting you." They smile faintly. Ren: "Now I think it means they trust you with doubt."
The player gives Ren one final lesson.
Kindness "Do not become cruel just because cruelty is efficient." Ren: "I'll remember that. Especially when efficiency sounds tempting."
Strength "Do not hesitate when people depend on you." Ren: "I'll become someone who can end things."
Wisdom "Do not give truth to people who only know how to weaponize it." Ren: "I'll learn when to speak and when to seal my mouth."
Freedom "Do not let any of us finish writing you." Ren looks out at the island. Ren: "Then I'll be unfinished on purpose."
Mission rewards are granted. Captain Iori gives the final line. Captain Iori: "A Genin survives orders. A Chunin carries them. A leader questions what those orders make of everyone beneath them."

In a dark archive, another copy of Ren's page is placed inside a black folder. A masked figure writes one sentence beneath the old evaluation: "Subject's development has accelerated. Continue observation." Mission ends.
objectives.successDescription: The Ember Ledger is recovered, Kaito Vey is defeated, and Ren leaves the mission changed by the player's command choices.

data.name: Strange Tastes
data.description: Something’s gone wrong with a new “culinary innovation” commissioned by McRamen. The laboratories insist it’s nothing dangerous… just a small experimental mishap. Still, shinobi are asked for assistance before word spreads and the problem gets out of hand. Track down the runaway creation and secure it before anyone else gets hurt
data.successDescription: You have successfully captured the rogue Triceranuggy. Dr. Kim’s research can now continue, and the village can rest a little easier. But whispers remain—if one nugget could roam free, others surely lurk in the shadows. This victory is only the first bite in a much larger feast of chaos.

objectives.description: At the mission hall, you find the familiar figure of the quest giver, a woman whose presence feels like both command and shadow. Her eyes linger on you with sharp amusement, as though she already knows you’ll accept before you even open your mouth.

So, you’ve come. Good. I have a task… unusual, but necessary. McRamen’s latest scheme to ‘improve flavor’ has gone awry. Their tinkering birthed… things that were never meant to walk this world. You are needed in Dr. Kim’s lab. Go, and hear the details from them. Consider this your first taste of the chaos they’ve stirred.

You set out through the village streets, where the golden arches of McRamen loom from every ramen stall like watchful eyes. Whispers follow you—rumors of strange sightings near the outskirts, animals that were never animals at all. The air smells faintly of fried batter and ozone. You have to reach the Lab before things escalate further.

Thank the gods you’re here! I… may have made a small miscalculation. McRamen wanted a compound to ‘enhance authenticity.’ Dr. Kim made the initial formula but… I tried to improve it and well… when applied to their test batch of chicken nuggets…

…well, they became authentic in ways no one intended. Living, breathing… prehistoric. I require your help. One of them, a triceratops-like specimen, was spotted nearby. I will give you the coordinates. Please subdue it and send it here. My research depends on it.
One more thing… I think my formula made these nuggets absorb any chakra they find in nature… We’re not sure yet how far they’ve taken these abilities.

Not far from the lab, you come upon torn-up earth and deep impressions pressed into the mud. The tracks are oddly familiar—like an elephant or rhinoceros—but broader, heavier, and scattered with crumbs of breading.

You follow the trail through thinning woods until the sound of chewing reaches your ears. Ahead, a squat creature with a breaded hide and tiny, glistening eyes gnaws on a patch of grass. Steam wafts from its body as though it had just left the fryer. The Triceranuggy raises its head, noticing you.
The creature gobbles down the offering, then suddenly glows. Its body hardens, its horns sharpen, and the triceratops nugget roars, twice its previous strength.
The nugget charges at you, stubborn but manageable in its current form.

You got her back!!! N-not that I doubted your skills of course but... I was worried. Thank you! With this we... we can figure out how to reverse the effects of the serum!

data.name: The Tower of Endless Night: Dawnless Crown

data.name: The Shattered Sakura: Part 1 - A Burdened Farewell
data.description: Whispers of a regional conflict between Shirohana and Akikaze have finally reached your ears, though the main villages seem largely unaffected. However, a small, independent nation, the Sakura Bloom Clan, has been caught in the crossfire. A somber request has arrived from Lord Kazuki: his daughter, Princess Yumi, must be escorted to safety near Hyorin. You are tasked with meeting her retainer, a seasoned Chunin, at a designated rendezvous point near the edge of the Misty Morass, and beginning the perilous journey. This mission is about protection, not glory.
data.successDescription: You successfully protected Princess Yumi and Takashi from desperate bandits, beginning the arduous escort mission. More importantly, you witnessed Princess Yumi's first fragile words, revealing the loss of her mother's cherished cherry blossom pin—a crucial step towards understanding her emotional pain and a potential turning point in her healing.

objectives.description: Travel to the rendezvous point (Edge of Misty Morass) in Sector 212

The air is thick with mist and the tension of waiting. Takashi, a Chunin with weary eyes, paces nervously, clutching a scroll. He turns sharply as you approach, then relaxes slightly, recognizing you.

"You are the shinobi sent by... good. There's no time for pleasantries. We've been through hell. Lord Kazuki sends his urgent plea for assistance. The Princess… she must be taken to safety. Here." (He thrusts the scroll into your hand.) "The war between Shirohana and Akikaze devastated our lands. Our village is a ruin. She's all that's left of our hope."
Collect Lord Kazuki's Letter

You receive Lord Kazuki's urgent letter. (Reading it: The letter details the destruction of the Sakura Bloom Clan's lands caught between the Shirohana-Akikaze conflict, and a rival clan, the Iron Claw, now threatens what little remains. Princess Yumi must be escorted to a sanctuary near Hyorin. Instructions are vague on the path, prioritizing speed and discretion.)

Takashi gestures to a small figure huddled beside a twisted tree. Princess Yumi, a young girl with disturbingly blank eyes, clutches a worn wooden doll. She doesn't look at you, her gaze fixed on the misty distance.
(Takashi speaks, his voice heavy with sorrow.) "Princess Yumi. She… she hasn’t spoken much since the raid. We need to move to the Abandoned Outpost in sector 261. It should be safer, for now."

nextObjectiveId.text: (Attempt to speak to Yumi gently.) "Hello, Princess. My name is..."

objectives.description: Escort Princess Yumi and Takashi to the Abandoned Outpost in sector 261. The journey is quiet, save for the rustling leaves and Yumi's faint footsteps.

You attempt to speak to Yumi, but she doesn't respond, her gaze unwavering, her grip on the doll tightening slightly. Takashi places a gentle hand on your shoulder. "She… she hasn’t responded since the last raid. She saw too much. Just focus on getting her to safety in sector. That's all that matters now."

(Takashi lets out a tired sigh.) "We are safe here for now. Lord Kazuki believes the Iron Claw Clan, a rival nation, is exploiting the chaos left by Shirohana and Akikaze to expand their influence. They would take Yumi to sever our line. He insists she go to Hyorin for now. It breaks his heart, but her safety is paramount. We need to reach the forest path soon, but something feels… off."

nextObjectiveId.text: We should rest briefly then move.

objectives.description: Suddenly, a branch snaps outside. Voices, coarse and cruel, can be heard approaching. "Heard rumors of a rich prize passing through this sector... might be that little princess."....  (Takashi's eyes widen in alarm.) "Bandits! They found us! Protect the Princess!"
Rogue Shinobi, desperate bandits, attack the outpost! Protect Princess Yumi and Takashi!
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to protect Princess Yumi and Takashi from the bandits. The mission is severely compromised.

objectives.description: With the bandits defeated, Takashi quickly checks on Yumi. She remains silent, but her body trembles. Takashi looks at you, grim. "Close call. These rogues are everywhere now, desperate after the war. This path is more dangerous than I thought. We need to move, now, and get to the Forest Path in sector 306. The sooner we reach safety, the better. No more delays."

nextObjectiveId.text: Agreed. Let's get to the Forest Path.
(Look at Yumi with concern.) "I think she needs comfort."

objectives.description: You continue the escort, moving carefully along the Forest Path. The dense canopy makes it hard to see, but also provides cover. Go to sector 306.

You glance at Yumi. She slowly, imperceptibly, reaches out a small hand and lightly grasps Takashi's sleeve. She still doesn't speak, but it's a small sign of connection. Takashi offers you a faint, grateful nod. "Even in silence, her spirit endures. She needs us now more than ever. We must protect that small ember."

You walk for some time in the quiet, shadowed forest. Suddenly, Yumi stops. She slowly reaches into her simple kimono and pulls out her wooden doll. Her eyes, still wide, finally seem to focus, not on you, but on the doll. A faint, almost lost whisper escapes her lips."...Mama... The cherry blossom… pin…"

(Takashi looks at you, surprised. This is the first she’s spoken.) "The cherry blossom pin? Her mother’s gift. She always wore it. It was lost during the raid, I think... It brought her comfort. It's a small, intricate pin, made of polished wood and silver, shaped like a blooming sakura, believed to have minor protective properties."

Princess Yumi has finally spoken, revealing her distress and the loss of a cherished, protective item—her mother's cherry blossom pin. This small connection to her past could be key to healing her spirit, but retrieving it means risking further danger.

nextObjectiveId.text: It must be important to her. We need to find it.
We don't have time to search. Her safety is more important.

objectives.description: We have a ghost. 'Sparrow' has fled with everything. His knowledge could burn our entire network to the ground. He has surfaced in the neutral port city of Kaiyo. Go there. Travel to the neutral port city of Kaiyo and find a vantage point on the rooftops to begin your search.

The city is a sprawling maze, but your training allows you to see what others miss. On a distant water tower, you spot a faint chakra seal—a directional marker from an old ANBU cipher. Sparrow is arrogant. He's using our own methods to lay his trail.
The trail ends, pointing down towards a nondescript tea house in a shadowy alley. This is the place.

You slip inside. The air is still. You immediately spot three pressure plates, a nearly invisible tripwire connected to a poison dart trap, and a genjutsu seal on the main door designed to induce paranoia. You carefully disarm and navigate the traps, moving deeper into the building.

You find Sparrow sitting calmly in the back room. "I knew you'd come," he says, not turning around. "But Command is still using the old protocols. Predictable." He rises, his eyes glowing with malevolent chakra. "Let's see if the new generation is any better.

data.name: The Wind Beneath the Ruins
data.description: A reconstruction survey in the Ruins of Current found tracks that belong to neither animal nor shinobi. Join Master Joren and his Genin team, enter the abandoned village, and find what is moving beneath the stones.
data.successDescription: The survey returns to Akikaze with proof that something from Current's past is still active beneath the ruins.

objectives.description:
Morning comes softly over Akikaze. Silver light moves across the Windswept Grasslands while the wind threads through the wooden towers of the eastern gate.

A young Genin waits beneath the gate in a coat that looks suspiciously newer than the dust rubbed into its sleeves. Above him, a girl with a cloth over the lower half of her face sits on the railing.

"You are late," she says.

"The sun has barely risen," Sorei replies.

"It rose three minutes ago."

"That is not how time works."

"It is exactly how time works."

nextObjectiveId.text: Wait for the rest of the team.

objectives.description:
Master Joren approaches with the slow, unhurried pace of a man who expects the road to wait for him. Behind him comes Riku, a broad-shouldered Genin carrying enough food for a much longer journey.

Sorei eyes the pack. "What is in there?"

"Supplies."

"For what?"

"The mission."

"We are going for one day."

Riku frowns. "People get hungry in one day."

Mika glances toward you. "I told them we should have brought a dog."

Joren walks between everyone without comment. "Walk."

Akikaze disappears behind rolling hills until only the tops of its watchtowers remain. Oakwood Forest darkens the western horizon, while the northern valleys rise toward country where the wind can tear young trees from the earth.

"Where exactly are we going?" Riku asks around a mouthful of breakfast.

Joren does not slow. "The Ruins of Current."

Sorei looks north. "My grandfather used to say a village does not disappear when its walls fall. It disappears when its children forget its name."

Mika studies him for a moment. "He said cheerful things, did he?"

"Not often."

Shortly before midday, the road reaches a low ridge. Below lie the bones of Current. Grass has swallowed old streets and collapsed houses. Broken walls rise from the fields like weathered teeth, and one split tower leans over the eastern road.

Wind passes through the empty windows with a sound somewhere between a whistle and a sigh. Riku stops eating.

Mika looks down into the ruins. "What exactly are we doing here?"

"Three nights ago a reconstruction team surveyed the northern quarter," Joren says. "They found tracks."

"Animal?"

"No."

"Shinobi?"

"No."

Joren watches the ruins. "That is why we are here."

The old road into Current is paved with pale stone broken by roots and weeds. Faded symbols remain on several slabs. Mika kneels beside one and brushes away the dirt.

"This one means shelter."

Joren glances down. "Almost."

Mika frowns.

"Refuge," he says.

"There is a difference?"

"There usually is."

The team moves deeper between the broken buildings.

The deeper the team goes, the quieter the ruins become. The grass continues to bend. Loose cloth stirs at Sorei's sleeve. Yet no wind touches your face.

Sorei stops. Mika takes two more steps before looking back.

"What?"

He raises a hand and watches the grass. "The wind."

Riku looks around. "What about it?"

nextObjectiveId.text: Study the air around the team.

objectives.description:
The motion is unmistakable. Wind crosses the ruined street, divides around the team, and joins again beyond it without touching the space between.

Sorei's eyes track the moving grass. "It is going around us."

Joren turns slowly toward the collapsed buildings ahead.

Mika's voice drops. "Wind does not avoid people."

"No," Joren says. "It avoids something else."

Clink.

Something shifts beneath the earth.

Riku lowers his pack. Mika's hand settles on the kunai at her thigh.

Clink.

Closer.

At the end of the street, a roofless building sags beneath its own beams. The darkness below them looks deeper than the space should allow. Something scrapes against stone.

Joren raises two fingers. The Genin spread out.

A hand presses out of the darkness beneath the collapsed building.

It is not armored. It is metal.

Five narrow fingers close around the old stone, followed by an arm plated in black. Sand pours from its joints as something drags itself from beneath the ruins. Its head emerges last: a smooth dark mask with a single pale light opening at its center like an eye.

The machine rises higher than anyone in the street.

Symbols have been cut into the machine's chest. Sorei stares at one of them and goes still.

"I know that mark," he says. "My grandfather carved it into the box he carried out of Current."

The pale eye turns toward him and brightens.

"Sorei," Joren says quietly.

The machine takes one step forward. Stone cracks beneath its foot.

Joren moves between it and the Genin. "Whatever you are thinking, think about it later."

The machine raises one arm. Wind rushes suddenly through the street, pulling dust from the stones. Pale light gathers inside the open metal palm.

Sorei reaches for his kunai. Mika lowers her stance. Riku drops the pack and finally stops worrying about breakfast.

Joren does not look back.

"Move!"

objectives.drawDescription: The fight with the Current Sentinel ends without a victor.
objectives.failDescription: The Current Sentinel forces the team back through the ruins.
objectives.fleeDescription: You withdraw from the Current Sentinel.

objectives.description:
The Sentinel drives the team back between the broken walls. Joren catches Sorei by the shoulder and pulls him clear as the pale light gathers again.

"Reset your footing," Joren says. "We do this together."

The Sentinel finally collapses. Its pale eye flickers once, twice, and goes dark.

For one breath the ruins are perfectly still. Then the wind returns all at once. Dust lifts from the street, grass bends through the broken foundations, and loose cloth snaps sharply in the moving air.

Riku looks down at the machine. "Can I eat now?"

Mika nudges one metal finger with her boot. "Ask it."

Joren crouches beside the chest plate. "Nobody touches anything until we know what woke it."

Sorei kneels beside the dark chest plate but keeps his hands away from it.

"It is the same mark," he says. "Exactly the same."

Joren studies the symbol, then removes a loose fragment from the shattered outer plate and wraps it in cloth.

"Then the reconstruction survey is over. This is an investigation now."

His gaze moves across the buried foundations surrounding the street.

"One machine came out because we walked over it. We do not know how many more are still asleep."

nextObjectiveId.text: Leave the ruins with the evidence.

objectives.description:
The ruins fall behind as the team returns toward Akikaze. Sorei is quieter than he was that morning. After a long while, he touches the new mark at his forehead.

"I thought earning this meant I was ready."

Joren keeps walking. "No. It means someone decided you were ready to carry responsibility. Those are not the same thing."

Mika glances sideways at Sorei. "You looked less nervous when the machine was trying to kill us."

"I was busy."

Riku shoulders his pack again. "So can we eat now?"

Joren sighs. "Walk."

objectives.successDescription: The team returns to Akikaze with a fragment of the machine and a warning: something built beneath Current survived the village that made it.
