data.name: The Ashen Lung
data.description: The mining settlement of Ironvein is choking. Miners from the newly opened eastern shaft have come up coughing black dust, grey-lipped, their chests rattling, unable to draw a full breath. As a medical specialist you must diagnose the affliction, deduce and gather the components for a drawing poultice, and treat the miners before the shaft claims them.
data.successDescription: The poultice draws the black dust from the miners' lungs. Their breathing eases, the grey fades from their lips, and Ironvein breathes again, the eastern shaft sealed until it can be made safe. Your sharp medical mind saved the settlement.

objectives.description: A soot-streaked foreman meets you at the gate, his voice a dry rasp. "Thank the spirits, a healer. My miners came up from the new eastern shaft coughing black dust, and now they can't draw a full breath. Grey lips, rattling chests. None of our healers has seen its like. Please, find what's stealing the air from their lungs."

You examine a stricken miner. His lips are ashen grey, his breath a shallow wet rattle, and when he coughs a fine black residue stains his hand. No fever, no swelling, nothing fights back. This is not a sickness running its course; it is a system being slowly smothered. What is your initial diagnosis?
"Something they breathed, not something they caught." Tetsu nods grimly. "That fits, and it was the diggers on the new eastern shaft who dropped first, before anyone else took ill. Where do we look?"
You descend into the new eastern shaft, lantern guttering in the close, dust-thick air.
Deep at the shaft face you find the source: a dark seam weeping a fine black dust into every breath of air. You seal a sample in a vial for analysis.
The dust is no living pathogen. It is a fine mineral grit, coating the lungs and smothering them from within. Force will not cough it loose. What is the correct medical approach?

nextObjectiveId.text: Draw It Out With a Poultice

objectives.description: You leave the shaft to seek a drawing agent, a deposit of fine medicinal clay along the old riverbank.
Along the cutbank you find a vein of pale, cool clay, the kind that pulls poison from a wound. You gather a portion.
The clay will draw the grit, but the miners' airways are raw and clenched tight. You need a third agent to soothe the lining and open the breath. What do you add to the poultice?
You work the cool clay, the cooling mint, and the bound black dust into a thick grey salve. The Ashvein Poultice is ready. It will draw the mineral from the lungs and ease the airways open.
You carry the finished poultice back up the shaft and through the gates of Ironvein.

You pack the poultice across the miners' chests and steep it in steam. Within the hour the black rattle softens, grey lips flush back to pink, and the first full breath in days rises around you. Tetsu grips your arm, eyes wet. "You gave them back the air. Ironvein won't forget it."

data.name: Where Winter's Weave Lies Still
data.description: Urgent news has reached you. The nest of the Spider Queen that has haunted Yukigumo Village has finally been found. Now it falls to you to descend into the depths and end the horror that has plagued this frozen land once and for all.
data.successDescription: You emerge into the frozen tundra, battered and bruised but victorious. This is it. The nest beneath the frost lies purged, its horrors silenced. The village will sleep peacefully now. Or so they believe.

objectives.description: I know you’re no stranger to the horrors that dwell in the cold… but we ask you to step up once more. The lair of the Spider Queen has been found, and with your record against her cult, you’re the only one we can count on.

nextObjectiveId.text: What do I have to do?

objectives.description: Head out once more to Yukigumo Village. The scouts stationed there have located the lair and will brief you further. Be safe, pack your gear… and come back in one piece.

The path feels familiar beneath your feet. You’ve walked it before. Yet this time, the cold seeps in long before you reach the village, sharper and heavier, as if the land itself knows what waits ahead.
objectives.successDescription: You reach Yukigumo Village once more. The memory of your last survival clings to you like frostbite. You can only hope that this time, your resolve will be enough to see you through again.

objectives.description: You're here. Good. The queen's lair has been found. The Queen’s lair has been found. We’re keeping the civilians safe and sweeping the outskirts for any remaining cultists.

nextObjectiveId.text: Have you checked the lair yet?

objectives.description: It’s a maze down there. Twisting tunnels, looping paths. People go in and never come back the same… if they come back at all. Keep your wits about you, and mark your way carefully

objectives.successDescription: You finally see it. The entrance yawning before you, black as the void and rimmed with frost. The Spider’s lair… hidden so close all this time. How many vanished souls found this same descent before you? You steel yourself and step into the dark below.

objectives.description: The tunnel opens into a vast cavern bathed in faint, shimmering light. A bed of pale blue flowers glows on the stone floor, life blooming where it shouldn’t. Faint daylight filters through a crack far above, glinting on the ice. Two tunnels lie ahead, each swallowing the light whole.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.

You press on, the passage narrowing until you must stoop to pass. The cold burns your lungs. When it finally widens, you find yourself before a ring of faintly glowing mushrooms, their light breathing softly against the stone. Ahead, three openings wait, black and hungry.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.

You follow the tunnel, its twists and turns leading you steadily upward. At last, a sharp crack of light greets you. You push through loose stone and ice, only to emerge once more into the frozen surface above. The storm greets you like an old friend. You’ve circled back.

nextObjectiveId.text: Descend into the tunnels once more.

objectives.description: It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.

This path feels older than the rest. The walls are scarred, clawed, and pitted. In the next cavern, a lone skeleton sits frozen against the wall, its armor shattered, its sword still clutched tight. The air feels colder here, heavier with memory.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.

A faint trickle of water echoes ahead. You come to a shallow stream running through the tunnel, clear and impossibly cold. Tiny shards of ice drift lazily across its surface. On the far side, three more paths wait, half-shrouded in mist.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.

The cold sharpens as you descend deeper. Your breath hangs heavy in the air. Strands of web begin to glisten along the stone walls, delicate and quivering. The silence grows unbearable. You can feel it, something vast and patient is near. Ahead, three paths yawn open.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.
It feels like the path you’ve taken has doubled back on itself.

You press forward, and the tunnel begins to spiral. The web grows thicker until it coats every surfac, walls, ceiling, floor, muffling even your breath. The air grows close, suffocating, heavy with dread. Somewhere ahead, something skitters, slow and deliberate. The passage widens into a cavern veiled in silk.

The cavern is immense. Sheets of silk hang from the ceiling like tattered banners, swaying in a chill current that shouldn’t exist. Faint blue light pulses through veins of chakra that weave across the floor, forming a living web beneath your feet. Between the curtains of silk, a shadow stirs, massive, graceful, deliberate.  Then comes her voice: ancient and rasping, like winter wind whispering through a graveyard of ice. A soft, humorless titter echoes, followed by words that coil through the dark.

The silk stirs. From the shadowed ceiling, she descends—an enormous arachne, her upper body crowned in bone-white armor, her eyes gleaming with cold intelligence. The lower half of her body gleams with frostbitten chitin, her legs clicking against the web-strung stone.  Her laughter fractures the silence.
Naughty little youngling... you’ve slaughtered my children, trespassed in my sanctum. But this, this is where you meet your end.

objectives.description: You emerge into the frozen tundra, battered but victorious. The nest beneath the frost is finally purged. The village may rest easier now, though the silence of winter leaves you wondering if horrors ever truly sleep.

The left tunnel slopes down gently, the air growing heavy and still. You find a small underground pond, its surface frozen smooth as glass. The silence here is absolute, no movement, no life. Whatever dwelled here is long gone.

data.name: Echoes in the Gust II: Voices Below
data.description: Akikaze Village summons you after disturbances shake its sky-bridges and sacred wind channels. Uncover the Grounded Spiral, survive the aerial assault, and discover what still echoes in the gust.
data.successDescription: You defended Akikaze, restored the source wind channel, and helped the village recover a forgotten part of its history.

objectives.description: Maemi: “This is a founder’s capsule. These were left by the first survivors who climbed from the ruins of Samui and built what would become Akikaze. If our enemies carried this, they are not simply attacking our village. They are attacking our memory.”
The capsule shows refugees fleeing Samui through a raging storm. The founder speaks of survival and ascent—then the recording is interrupted by a masked figure.
Veyra: “Akikaze forgot the ground it abandoned. You built temples in the clouds and called it wisdom. But every platform hangs from something. Every wind has a source. We will cut yours.”
Maemi: “The threat is direct. If they know our wind channels, they can endanger every platform. Outsider, continue this investigation with Saeji and Councilor Iroha.”
Descend into the ochre dust and bronze vents of the Dust Maelstrom. A founder inscription near the central vent has been freshly scratched away.
Iroha: “Payment? During a village-wide sabotage threat? Charming. Survive, save the channels, and I may recommend enough hazard compensation to buy one bootlace in Akikaze.”
The investigation reaches Akikaze’s oldest training chamber, where someone has carved directly into the village’s founding record.
objectives.successDescription: The investigation reaches Akikaze’s oldest training chamber, where someone has carved directly into the village’s founding record.

objectives.description: Your decision disrupts the investigation or delays Akikaze’s defense. The Grounded Spiral escapes with stolen wind-channel data, and the source channel enters emergency lockdown. The village survives for now, but the truth remains buried beneath broken chimes and restless wind.

data.name: Copies, Not Thefts
data.description: Three of the Kage's letters were copied, not stolen. Get inside a private archive, take back the files, and bring home the ledger that names the buyer. How quietly you do it is up to you.
data.successDescription: Congratulations! You've successfully won the battle

objectives.description:
The briefing room is lit by one lantern over the map table. The Commander does not sit.

"Three of the Kage's letters left this village and came back as copies. Copies, not thefts. Someone wanted us blind, not angry.
The paper traces to a private archive that keeps records for anyone who pays."

nextObjectiveId.text: Why is ANBU not handling this openly?

objectives.description:
She sets a marker on the map, well outside the wall.

"That is what you will find out. Bring back what they hold and the ledger that says who paid. Nobody knows you were there.
One detail, since you will be reading their shelves: that archive files by season, not by year. Anyone who asks for a year has never been inside."

nextObjectiveId.text: And if the door is watched?

objectives.description:
The mission clerk has your kit ready before you reach the counter.

"Lockpicks, ink kit, two smoke tags, and a writ that will not survive a careful reader.
Sign here. Not with your real name, obviously."
Cross to the archive district under dark.

The safehouse smells of cold tea. Through the shutter slat you can see the archive door across the alley.

Two guards, one circuit, four minutes apart. There will be a service way in around the back, and a roof line if you would rather be quick than careful.
Work the alley behind the archive and map the ways in.

Three ways in, and the patrol turns in ninety seconds.

The coal chute is filthy, blind and slow. The roof line is quick and completely exposed. The front door would take the writ and a steady face.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the coal chute. Slow and unseen.
Go over the roof line. Fast and loud.

objectives.description: Crawl the coal chute, one shoulder at a time, and drop into the cellar.

You come out under the stacks with soot in your teeth and nobody the wiser.

Above you the building is quiet in the way that means everyone in it believes they are alone.

The tiles are wet and one of them moves under your foot.

Across the roof a lookout turns, sees you, and does not shout. He reaches for the bell rope instead, which is worse.
Take the lookout down before he reaches the rope.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description:
He does not reach it. But he got a hand to it, and somewhere below a small bell moved once.

One ring is not an alarm. It is a question. Someone in this building is already walking toward the answer.

nextObjectiveId.text: Get inside before they find it.

objectives.description:
The clerk reads the writ twice, which is once more than you wanted.

"Requisition, then. Which index do you need pulled?"

nextObjectiveId.text: The index for the year, all of it.
Whichever one the Kage's office uses.

objectives.description:
He nods, bored, and writes it down. Everyone who works here knows they file by season. Only outsiders ask for a year.

"Third aisle, and do not take the lamp past the ledgers."
He goes back to his tea. You walk into the archive through the front door like a man with business here.

He smiles, and the smile does not reach anything.

"We do not index by year. Never have."
The writ goes in his pocket, not back in your hand, and two men walk you out. By the time you are in the alley again the lamps are lit on the upper floor and the building knows it has a visitor.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go over the roof, then. Nothing quiet left to lose.

objectives.description:
Rows of shelving run back into the dark, every one packed with rolled paper.

Somewhere below, a single lamp is still burning. Seasons, not years. The autumn shelves are the far wall.
Search the seasonal shelves for the transfer ledger.

The ledger is ordinary until the last three pages.

Every transfer in the same neat hand, buyer left, price right. Your village letters are listed twice.
The name beside them is one you have heard in a briefing room, on the other side of the table.

nextObjectiveId.text: Copy the page and get the files.

objectives.description: Work the seal on the file drawer.

Someone has been in the room the whole time.

He steps out from between the shelves without hurrying, which is worse than if he ran. No crest, no colours, nothing to say who pays him. Only the way he stands, which says he has done this before.
objectives.drawDescription: Neither side yielded. The contract stands.
objectives.failDescription: They were stronger than the posting suggested. Regroup.

objectives.description: Take the ledger and the files out the way you came, and cross back over the border before first light.

The Commander reads the page twice, then sets it face down on the map.

"You were not seen. Good.
As for this name, you will forget you read it until I tell you to remember. That is not a request, and it is not for your protection."

data.name: The Ascension Ceremony
data.description: A new clan leader, Lady Suzume Aerathiel, has been chosen to ascend during Akikaze's sacred leadership ceremony. Before the rites can begin, an assassin infiltrates the preparations, kidnaps Suzume, and announces plans to execute her before the ceremony bell rings. Investigate the attack, track the assassin through Akikaze's ceremonial routes, and rescue the chosen leader before her ascension becomes a public tragedy.
data.successDescription: You have rescued Lady Suzume Aerathiel, defeated the assassin sent to execute her, and preserved the Ascension Ceremony. Akikaze's people witness their new clan leader rise not through unchallenged peace, but through survival, courage, and the unbroken flow of the wind.

objectives.description: Saeji of the Sky Wardens: “Lady Suzume Aerathiel is to ascend today as her clan's new leader. The pavilion is full, the banners are up, and every important person in Akikaze is pretending not to watch everyone else for weakness. In other words, a perfect day for someone to attempt something stupid, expensive, and treasonous.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Clan politics are not my concern.

objectives.description: Zephyr Kage Maemi: “This ceremony is more than tradition. The Aerathiel clan anchors much of Akikaze's wind mastery and military prestige. If Suzume is harmed before her ascension, the clan may fracture, and our enemies will smell weakness in the air.”
Inspect the Aerathiel Preparation Hall before Lady Suzume begins the procession.
objectives.successDescription: The hall is elegant and quiet. Lady Suzume stands before an ancestral mirror while attendants prepare her ceremonial mantle.

objectives.description: Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “So you are the one Saeji trusts when the wind turns sharp. Good. I would rather have honest eyes near me today than flattering mouths. Too many people celebrate an ascension while quietly measuring where the new leader may bleed.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Who would want to stop your ascension?
You seem calm for someone in danger.

objectives.description: Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Expect? No. Prepare for? Always. The Aerathiel name carries honor, influence, and old resentments. Some prefer a leader they can control. I am not built for leashwork.”

Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Rivals within the clan, enemies outside it, old families who dislike change, and perhaps someone offended by the tragic scandal of a woman with a spine. The list is long. The patience is short.”
Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Fear wastes breath. I may need mine later.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Let's make sure you keep it.

objectives.description: Escort Lady Suzume from the preparation hall toward the Wind-Chime Processional Path.
objectives.successDescription: The first chimes ring in proper sequence, but the third chime cracks instead of sounding. A smoke charm bursts among the attendants.

objectives.description: Masked infiltrators disguised as ceremonial attendants attack the procession, attempting to separate Suzume from her guards.
objectives.drawDescription: The deadlock consumes the remaining time before the ceremonial bell.
objectives.failDescription: The assassins overwhelm you, and the ceremony deadline slips away.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the pursuit, leaving Lady Suzume to the assassin.
objectives.successDescription: The smoke clears, but Lady Suzume is gone. Her silver hairpin lies on the stone, stained with pressure poison.

objectives.description: Saeji of the Sky Wardens: “They did not come to kill her here. They came to take her. The third chime was altered to mask a displacement gust. Someone planned this with temple timing and security knowledge.”
Elder Shion: “The procession chimes were not merely broken. They were made to ring out of sequence. To the crowd, it will look like the ceremony rejected her. That is the true wound they seek.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Announce the kidnapping to the crowd.

objectives.description: Follow the pressure poison residue and Suzume's scattered ceremonial thread toward the Festival Bridgeway.
objectives.successDescription: Civilians are confused by the delayed ceremony. A false attendant slips through the crowd carrying a hidden charm.

objectives.description: Master Harun Aerathiel: “This reeks of internal betrayal. Suzume's selection angered several lesser branches. But whoever took her moved like a hired blade, not a clan traditionalist. Find the hand holding the knife before accusing the hand that paid for it.”
A false attendant and hidden cutters attempt to delay your pursuit by causing panic on the Festival Bridgeway.
objectives.drawDescription: The deadlock consumes the remaining time before the ceremonial bell.
objectives.failDescription: The assassins overwhelm you, and the ceremony deadline slips away.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the pursuit, leaving Lady Suzume to the assassin.
objectives.successDescription: The false attendant drops an altered ropeway log tied to a hidden station beneath the ceremonial district.

objectives.description: Councilor Iroha: “This log has been rewritten with pressure-ink. Again. I swear, criminals discover one expensive trick and suddenly develop artistic confidence. The route leads to a hidden ropeway station under the pavilion.”
Descend beneath the ceremonial district and investigate the hidden ropeway station.
objectives.successDescription: The station's official seals have been cut. A ropeway carriage recently departed toward the outer platforms, leaving behind nearly invisible Split Gale wire.

objectives.description: Ropeway saboteurs attack to destroy the station controls and erase the assassin's route.
objectives.drawDescription: The deadlock consumes the remaining time before the ceremonial bell.
objectives.failDescription: The assassins overwhelm you, and the ceremony deadline slips away.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the pursuit, leaving Lady Suzume to the assassin.
objectives.successDescription: You recover Split Gale wire and partial route data pointing toward the Shattered Banner Platform.

objectives.description: Follow the ropeway route to the Shattered Banner Platform.
objectives.successDescription: Torn Aerathiel banners whip in the wind. Blood marks the stone, and an Execution Notice Charm hangs from a broken banner pole.

objectives.description: System Narration: “The charm activates as you approach. A woman's voice speaks through the wind: 'The chosen leader dies before the bell. Let Akikaze witness what false ascension earns.' The charm burns away, revealing the mark of the Split Gale.”

Saeji of the Sky Wardens: “Nyra of the Split Gale. Assassin, kidnapper, political butcher. She executes targets in symbolic locations so the death spreads farther than the body. If she has Suzume, she will choose somewhere visible, high, and cruel.”
Pursue Nyra along the old Assassin's Skyhook Route before the Ceremonial Wind Bell rings.
objectives.successDescription: The route is a deadly chain of cliffside hooks and narrow anchor points. Split Gale operatives cut loose support lines as you approach.

objectives.description: Fight through Split Gale operatives while crossing the unstable skyhook route.
objectives.drawDescription: The deadlock consumes the remaining time before the ceremonial bell.
objectives.failDescription: The assassins overwhelm you, and the ceremony deadline slips away.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the pursuit, leaving Lady Suzume to the assassin.
objectives.successDescription: The last cutter reveals that Nyra has taken Suzume to the Execution Spire above the cloudline.

objectives.description: Ascend to the Execution Spire before Nyra completes the public execution.
objectives.successDescription: Lady Suzume is bound with pressure-wire restraints near the edge of the spire. Nyra stands beside her holding Suzume's stolen clan seal. The distant Ceremonial Wind Bell begins to rise into position.

objectives.description: Nyra of the Split Gale: “A leader chosen by ceremony can be unmade by spectacle. When the bell rings, she falls. The people will not remember her policies, her bloodline, or her pretty speeches. They will remember that the wind rejected her.”

nextObjectiveId.text: The wind did not reject her. You staged a murder.

objectives.description: Nyra of the Split Gale: “Still pretending truth matters more than what the crowd believes? Precious. I almost feel bad charging extra for this.”
Nyra of the Split Gale: “Names are expensive. Yours is not the purse that paid me. Defeat me, perhaps I will leave enough evidence for your Council to panic over.”

nextObjectiveId.text: I'll take the evidence from you.

objectives.description: Nyra attacks with pressure-wire restraints, silent Wind Style movement, paralysis needles, and execution-stage traps. Defeat her before the Ceremonial Wind Bell rings.
objectives.drawDescription: The deadlock consumes the remaining time before the ceremonial bell.
objectives.failDescription: The assassins overwhelm you, and the ceremony deadline slips away.
objectives.fleeDescription: You abandon the pursuit, leaving Lady Suzume to the assassin.
objectives.successDescription: Nyra is defeated and drops Suzume's clan seal. The pressure-wire restraints remain active around Suzume.

objectives.description: System Narration: “The pressure wires tighten as the bell nears its final ring. Cutting them recklessly could trigger the execution trap.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Loosen the wires by matching their wind rhythm.
Use the clan seal to disrupt the trap.

objectives.description: Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “Steady. The wires respond to pressure, not force. Let them believe the wind has already moved past me.”
System Narration: “You press Suzume's clan seal against the restraint anchor. The seal's Aerathiel wind signature disrupts the trap, weakening the pressure wires enough to remove them safely.”
Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “My thanks. I would prefer my ascension not begin with being thrown off a spire. Dramatic, yes. Undignified, absolutely.”

nextObjectiveId.text: Let's get you back to the ceremony.

objectives.description: Escort Lady Suzume back to the Ascension Terrace before the ceremony is formally canceled.
objectives.successDescription: The crowd falls silent as Suzume appears alive, wounded but standing. The delayed Ceremonial Wind Bell rings across Akikaze.

objectives.description: Zephyr Kage Maemi: “Let all gathered witness: the ceremony was attacked, the chosen leader was taken, and still she returned. The wind does not favor those untouched by danger. It favors those who rise through it.”

Lady Suzume Aerathiel: “I was chosen before today. Now I have been tested before you all. Let my first vow as clan leader be this: no fear, no hired blade, and no hidden coward will decide the future of Aerathiel. We move with the wind, but we do not bow to those who poison it.”

Saeji of the Sky Wardens: “You saved the leader, exposed the assassin, and prevented a clan crisis. Not bad. Iroha says the damaged ropeway, broken chimes, and ruined banner platform will be added to your 'heroic inconvenience' file. Congratulations, Comrade. You are becoming expensive.”

System Narration: “Your decision delays the rescue or triggers the assassin's trap. Lady Suzume is executed before the Ascension Ceremony can be completed. The Aerathiel clan falls into turmoil, and Akikaze's sacred transition becomes a wound that enemies will exploit for years.”

data.name: Witness Detail
data.description: An hour before dawn a witness has to reach a hearing on the other side of the village, and the people who want her absent were paid to take her alive. Three ways across. All of them end in a fight.
data.successDescription: She reached the steps and she gave the name.

objectives.description:
The handler does not sit down, and does not offer you tea. She lays a folded contract on the table and turns it so the price faces you.

"Somebody bought her. Not her death, her absence. Take, was the word they used."

nextObjectiveId.text: Absence buys silence. Death buys questions.

objectives.description:
She does not agree out loud. She taps the table twice with one finger, the way you tap a wall in the dark to find the door.

"The last one I sent asked me why they had not simply killed her. Since you are quicker than him, keep up. The Unsigned chalk a lane before they work it, one stroke, low on the corner stone. Not a warning to you. A note they leave each other."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will read their notes.

objectives.description:
She looks up properly for the first time, and does not quite hide that she is reassessing you.

"Slowly, then. A body is a crime. Somebody has to investigate a crime, and investigating this one means reading the ledger she was going to talk about. A witness who simply fails to arrive is nobody's case at all. Now, the Unsigned chalk a lane before they work it. One stroke, low on the corner stone. It is not a warning meant for you, it is a note they leave each other."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then I will read their notes.

objectives.description:
Kanna is twenty two, has not slept, and holds a rolled statement against her chest like it is the only warm thing she owns.

"They came to my father's house first," she says. "They were very polite about it. That is the part I keep thinking about."

She is at the door with her coat already on, standing at your left shoulder like she was told. Past it the village is dark for another hour, and somewhere in that hour people are standing very still, waiting to be told which way the two of you went.

"You choose," she says. "I have been choosing all week and look where it put me."

nextObjectiveId.text: The market road. Loud rooms hide loud men.
The back lanes. Slow, blind, ours.
Give me your coat. You walk alone.

objectives.description: The market road is loud with carts before dawn, which is cover of a kind, and a hundred witnesses, which is not.

A fruit seller looks at you twice and then does not look at all. Two men come through the crowd at walking pace, because hurrying is what a crowd remembers.

"The polite one is on the left," Kanna says. Her voice does not shake, which is somehow worse.
Two of them working the crowd. Neither one looks at Kanna, which means each is counting on the other to reach her first.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The crowd closes over it before it has finished happening. She has not moved from behind your shoulder.

objectives.description: The back lanes take three times as long and cross no open ground at all. A patrol passes the lane mouth and you wait it out with her hand over her own mouth.

Chalk on the corner stone. One stroke, low down, unweathered. The rain stopped two hours ago.

"It is only chalk," Kanna whispers. "Children do that."

nextObjectiveId.text: Children do not chalk at midnight. Take the parallel.

objectives.description:
You take the parallel and leave theirs empty. Somewhere behind you a lane that somebody spent the evening preparing stays quiet all the way to dawn, and nobody standing in it ever learns why.

"Children," Kanna says, eventually. "Yes. That was stupid of me."
Not children. The lane was chalked because it is long, and blind, and opens at one end, and what is waiting at that end has been waiting a while.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: You get out of the lane. It costs you.

objectives.description:
The coat is tight across your shoulders and smells of her house. She takes the servants' stair without being told twice.

"If they take you instead of me," she says from the dark, "I am still going. I wanted you to know that first."
They send the good one after the coat. She works out that it is empty about four steps too late, and does not stop, because she was not paid to stop.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The coat is ruined. Kanna is three streets away and has not been touched.

objectives.description: The hearing hall stands at the top of eleven steps. The bell has not rung.

Someone has been sitting on the steps long enough that the frost has taken the shape of him. He stands at the exact distance where leaving stops being something you can do quietly.

"She has an hour," he says. "I only need her to miss it."

nextObjectiveId.text: Then you come through me first.

objectives.description: He takes you up on it without a word. No lane, no crowd, no coat. Eleven steps, and a bell about to ring.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: The bell rings on the second stroke of it. She walks up past you and does not look down.

objectives.description:
The clerk checks the hour before he checks her name, and writes them down in that order.

"If she had come in after the bell," he says, still writing, "I would have noted that instead, and there would be nothing here to hear. No crime in it. The record does not ask why a person was late."

nextObjectiveId.text: One hour. That was the whole price of her.

objectives.description: Witness delivered, statement taken.

You come to in a doorway with your collar gone stiff. Two doors down, behind the water butt, something that has been holding still for twenty minutes moves.

"I did what you told me," Kanna says. "The bell has not rung yet. Get up."
The safehouse, the lamp oil, the three ways across the village.

data.name: The Tale of Goah Way: The Girl Who Carried Two Storms
data.description: Goah Way follows whispers of black lightning and two women speaking through an impossible storm. At an abandoned watchtower he finds a girl carrying Eclipse's obsidian chakra and Aegis's violet lightning. Together they confront the surviving Unbroken Thread.
data.successDescription: The ancient vault is destroyed. The Unbroken Thread is broken. The girl who carried two storms chooses what her legacy will mean.

objectives.description: Rain falls beneath a clear sky. Merchants whisper of black lightning, ancient bones, and two women speaking through the storm. Goah Way adjusts his weathered pack and walks toward the eastern pass.
Reach Stormbreak Pass, where lightning crawls beneath the mountain.
A shattered watchtower overlooks the valley. A woman steps into the rain with obsidian chakra on one side of her body and violet lightning on the other. She says only: Leave.

nextObjectiveId.text: I am here because everyone calls you a monster.
I will not draw a weapon unless you do.

objectives.description: She asks whether Goah came to kill her. He sees the patched roof, the struggling garden, and a life built from hiding. Goah answers that he came to ask her name.
During a night of thunder, she speaks of Eclipse, whose chakra devoured light, and Aegis, who carried the voice of a dying storm god. Their final words were: Live for us. Carry the sky.

nextObjectiveId.text: Honor the women who came before her.

objectives.description: The woman remembers almost nothing of her childhood. Goah tells her that memory is not a prison unless frightened people build its walls.
The Unbroken Thread survived beneath the mountains. Its scavengers and zealots have found the heir carrying both bloodlines. Their ritual needs a living key.

nextObjectiveId.text: Stand beside her when the cult arrives.

objectives.description: The Unbroken Thread emerges from the rain wearing the faces of ordinary travelers. Their seals ignite around the watchtower.
objectives.drawDescription: The mountain refuses to name a victor.
objectives.failDescription: Defeat sends the storm-carrier back into the rain before the cult can be stopped.
objectives.fleeDescription: The trail disappears into thunder and black mist.

objectives.description: The cult drives Goah and the storm-carrier away from the watchtower. The rain gives them one more chance.
The cultists fall, but the mountain answers with a mechanical groan. The woman looks toward an ancient vault and says the ritual is already waking beneath the earth.

nextObjectiveId.text: Follow the trail into the hollow.

objectives.description: Enter the Rain Hollow and find the concealed vault entrance.
An ancient ritual guardian awakens as obsidian and violet chakra overlap at the vault door.
objectives.drawDescription: The mountain refuses to name a victor.
objectives.failDescription: Defeat sends the storm-carrier back into the rain before the cult can be stopped.
objectives.fleeDescription: The trail disappears into thunder and black mist.

objectives.description: The guardian forces the pair back through the rain. Return to the vault entrance before the old machine seals itself.

Inside the vault, the woman touches a broken pendant. Memory floods the chamber: Eclipse shielding her with bone, Aegis carrying lightning in both hands, and two sisters choosing protection over vengeance.

nextObjectiveId.text: Carry their promise into the machine core.

objectives.description: Reach the Machine Core Chamber before High Inquisitor Varos completes the extraction seal.
High Inquisitor Varos begins harvesting the inherited bloodlines. The storm-carrier steps forward, no longer asking permission to exist.
objectives.drawDescription: The mountain refuses to name a victor.
objectives.failDescription: Defeat sends the storm-carrier back into the rain before the cult can be stopped.
objectives.fleeDescription: The trail disappears into thunder and black mist.

objectives.description: Varos forces the group away from the machine core. The extraction seal is not complete yet.
Varos calls her stolen blood. Goah calls her a person. She looks at lightning in one hand and black chakra in the other. For the first time, the choice is hers.

nextObjectiveId.text: I will carry both storms—and give them my own name.
The past belongs to me now.

objectives.description: The vault collapses beneath the mountain. The Unbroken Thread vanishes into the storm it tried to command. Goah remembers only the girl who carried two storms and refused to let either be forgotten.
objectives.successDescription: The storm-carrier chooses her own name, and the sisters' legacy becomes a promise instead of a prison.

data.name: The Last Shadow: Chapter III — Toward Justice
data.description: The Shadow Beast is regenerating. Hold the shrine long enough for Raizen to restore the prison beneath the Valley of Echoes.
data.successDescription: You uncover the truth behind Raizen's escape, prevent an ancient catastrophe, and fight alongside the Global ANBU to contain a forgotten evil. History remembers the mission not as a manhunt, but as the day a fugitive saved the world.

objectives.description: Assist Raizen in restoring the ancient sealing array before the Shadow Beast fully regenerates.
objectives.successDescription: The sealing chains begin reconnecting as ANBU operatives defend the ritual.

objectives.description: Defeat the Shadow Beast one final time while the sealing ritual completes.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ends without containment.
objectives.failDescription: Your formation breaks beneath the enemy assault.
objectives.fleeDescription: You retreat before the objective is secured.
objectives.successDescription: The ancient seal reforms, imprisoning the Shadow Beast once more beneath the valley.

objectives.description: Commander Kael: “History will never know the truth. They'll remember you as an escaped convict… but I know better.”
Raizen Kurogane: “Sometimes the only way to save the world… is to let it hate you first.”
Return to Global ANBU Command Center to report the mission.
objectives.successDescription: The official report is rewritten under the highest classification level.

objectives.description: Commander Kael: “This operation will remain classified. Officially, we captured a fugitive. Unofficially… we survived because of him.”
System Narration: “The mission is sealed under the codename: The Last Shadow.”
Commander Kael: “Remember this lesson. Not every fugitive is running from justice. Sometimes… they're running toward it.”
The final seal fractures. Fall back to Raizen's ritual position and attempt containment again.
The truth is buried, the world survives, and Raizen Kurogane disappears into classified history.

objectives.description: You find yourself back at the entrance to the lagoon, your head spinning.

The Howling Hills earn their name before you ever see them: one long howl rolling down the slopes, answered by another, and another, until the dusk itself seems to have a throat. Travelers who lose their footing in this place lose the trail with it; fall in battle here and you will find yourself back at this marker, starting over.

Do you dare enter?
The Dark Wolf drops, and for one breath the slope is quiet. Then, somewhere upslope, a second howl answers the first. A third joins it. The kill did not end the hunt; it announced you.

You run where the trail allows and fight where it does not. The pack has your scent now and paces you through the bracken, grey shapes keeping level with you on both sides, never tiring, waiting for your breath to give first.

The hills fold into a cliffside and the trail splits beneath a decrepit sign, its carving long since weathered to guesses. Left, a cave mouth breathes cold air and a growl so deep you feel it through your boots. Right, worn steps climb into the wind, and the wind up there is shrieking. Behind you, the howling swells as larger shapes join the pack.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go left, into the Growling Grotto
Go right, up the Shrieking Steps
Against your better instincts, turn and fight.

objectives.description: The tunnel runs on ahead while Howlers pour in behind you, their voices flattening into shrieks against the narrowing stone. There is no width here for running. You will have to fight your way through.

The tunnel climbs to the surface, and you understand at last: all the shrieking on the wind was one voice, carried down the steps to greet you. The Banshee stands amid her gathering, and she has been expecting you.

objectives.description: A howl unlike the others cuts the air, higher and colder, and the pack parts to let its answer through: wolves the color of moonlight, huge and silent, circling in without a sound. The dark pack hunted you. These have come to finish it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Too late to turn back now!

objectives.description: The white wolves fall, and the howling stops all at once, every voice in the hills cut off mid-cry. In the silence, something vast rises against the moon on the ridge above, and when it howls, alone, every wolf left alive answers it as one.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face the Monster of the Moon

objectives.description: The Monster of the Moon falls, and the hills go quiet for the first time all night, truly quiet, no throat left willing to answer the dark. The pack will not hunt these trails again soon.

Death's Maw collapses at the grotto's heart, and the growl you felt through your boots dies with it. In the new quiet, daylight shows grey at the cave's far mouth, and the way out of the hills is yours.
The Banshee's last shriek breaks against the steps and does not come back. The wind over the hills blows clean and wordless, and the high road stands open.

data.description: Goah Way, a peaceful wandering sage, is enjoying the sights of a bustling town. However, as dusk falls, he takes a shortcut through a dimly lit alley and finds his path blocked by a malicious ninja with sticky fingers. Guide Goah through this perilous encounter.
data.successDescription: You made it back to your lodging, shaken but safe. The experience was frightening, but it has reinforced your resolve. The world is full of shadows, but your path is to praise the sun. The journey continues, now with a valuable lesson in vigilance.

objectives.description: The day was wonderful, filled with new sights and friendly faces. But as the sun sets, you decide to take a shortcut back to your lodging through a quiet alleyway. The feeling of being watched has been nagging at you all day...
Head through the narrow alleyway.

A figure steps from the shadows, blocking your path. His masked face and malicious eyes leave no doubt as to his intentions. "Well, well, what do we have here?" he sneers. "Paper-thin arms and a heavy-looking bag. Today must be my lucky day. Hand over your valuables, and I might let you walk away."

nextObjectiveId.text: I will not. You'll have to take them from me.
Look for an opening to escape.
(Give Up) "Fine, take them. Just don't hurt me."

objectives.description: Brave words for a man who looks like he'd lose a fight to a strong breeze!" He lunges, his blade flashing!
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: The ninja lunges! As you dodge, you notice a glimmer of light reflecting off a nearby window. You remember the small, reflective disc a merchant gave you earlier. This could be your chance!

nextObjectiveId.text: (Use Disc) Fling the reflective disc at the ninja's face
(Hesitate) "I don't know... maybe I should just fight."

objectives.description: The ninja's blade is too fast. You fall, and he rifles through your belongings, taking everything of value. "Should've just praised the sun from your own backyard, old man," he sneers before melting back into the shadows, leaving you with nothing but scrapes and wounded pride.

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: You manage to land a lucky blow, knocking the ninja off balance. He stumbles back, surprised by your tenacity, giving you a chance to flee.

objectives.description: With a flick of your wrist, you send the disc flying. It catches the last rays of sunlight, creating a brilliant flash that blinds the ninja! "Agh! My eyes!" he curses. You don't waste a second, turning and sprinting down the alley.
The ninja is recovering quickly! You hear his footsteps pounding the pavement behind you. You spot a decrepit building with a door slightly ajar. Hide inside!

You slip inside, pulling the door shut as quietly as possible. Holding your breath, you listen as the ninja's footsteps approach, pause right outside, and then continue on, followed by a frustrated curse. You are safe.

You made it back to your lodging, shaken but safe. The experience was frightening, but it has reinforced your resolve. The world is full of shadows, but your path is to praise the sun. The journey continues, now with a valuable lesson in vigilance.

data.name: [Path of Crimson] [Part III: Chains of Deception]
data.description:
There's something wrong.

The moment you step onto Wake Island, you feel it. The air is heavy, thick with the lingering scent of burned wood, but it’s more than that. It’s the silence. The way the ocean barely stirs against the docks. The way the distant embers on the mainland still glow, flickering like open wounds across the land.

And then there’s Dusk.

He stands where he always does, near the island’s edge, his golden scarf resting against his shoulders instead of shifting with the wind. He doesn’t greet you with his usual smirk. He doesn’t say anything at all—not at first. When he finally does speak, it’s slower. Measured. Less like an old friend and more like someone choosing their words carefully.

“It’s worse than I expected.”

His gaze doesn’t leave the horizon. Even as he gestures toward the burned parchment on the nearby table, his fingers move almost mechanically, without the usual casual confidence.

“The Maw isn’t just raiding anymore. They’re following a pattern. Marking sites. The Ember Trail was only the beginning.”

On the map, two locations are circled in deep red ink. His hand lingers over them for a moment longer than necessary.

“If they finish what they’ve started, we’re out of time. We need to act first.”

And then—finally—he looks at you. But something is missing.

The usual sharp glint in his eyes isn’t there. His expression is neutral, his posture stiff, too still.

For the first time since you met him, Dusk looks like he’s waiting. Not just for your answer, but for your reaction.

“Destroy their operations. Take anything they were using. If they’re preparing something bigger, I want to know what it is.”

His voice is steady, but there’s something beneath it. Not doubt. Not hesitation. Just… calculation.

And then, softer—

“…And don’t hesitate. If you run into resistance, you know what to do.”

That, at least, sounds like him. But somehow, it makes everything else feel even stranger.

He hands you the map, his fingers brushing against yours for just a second longer than they should. It’s barely noticeable. But when he pulls away, he does it just a little too deliberately.

“Go. We don’t have time to waste.”

And with that, he turns back to the horizon, as if dismissing the conversation entirely. But for the first time, you’re not sure if he’s watching the burning sky—

—or making sure you’re leaving.

objectives.description: To the world, Dusk is still missing. But you know more than most—you saw him change, saw him fly away into the twilight.  If he left anything behind, it would be here. His shack, simple and weathered, stands waiting. You steel yourself, and push the door open.
The room smells faintly of smoke and ink. Dust coats the shelves, yet everything feels deliberate. Three things stand out among the clutter, each too carefully placed to be forgotten.
The desk is strewn with broken chopsticks and lacquer shavings. Only one piece is whole: two lacquered sticks tied with red ribbon, blossoms that never wilt, their edges smoldering faintly.
A small, corrupted creature snores in the corner. It looks twisted, but strangely at peace.
A worn field guide lies open on the desk. It’s signed “Jaktik,” but the handwriting is unmistakably Dusk’s.
Lifting the Memento reveals a burn-shadow scorched into the wood — blossoms outlined, with one hex seared deeper than the rest.

The guide lies open, margins filled with Jaktik’s notes. One page shows a rough map of Seichi with a single spot circled hard in ink. The entry beside it reads: Redhour Blossom — blooms rarely, but here it opens every sunset without fail. Petals flare crimson, then fade. I lingered too long. Something in me moved with them. The horizon felt alive.

The Hollowfoot dozes softly. Around its neck hangs a circular charm, worn smooth. On the front, etched in block letters: LEFTY. You turn it over — the back is carved with a crude map, a cluster of hexes with one marked clearly. It matches the shape of Seichi’s world map.

data.name: The Lost Wind
data.description: One of Akikaze's primary wind currents has vanished without warning, cutting power to nearly thirty percent of the village. Investigate the missing current, trace the disruption through Akikaze's turbine network, and restore the lost wind before the blackout spreads.
data.successDescription: You have restored the missing wind current, stabilized the main power station, and uncovered the hidden cause behind the disruption.

objectives.description: Councilor Iroha - Main Power Station: Thirty percent of the village has lost power because one of our primary wind currents has vanished. Winds do not simply disappear. Help me find out what happened.
Toma the Turbine Keeper - Main Power Station: The western turbines lost the current instantly. It was not a gradual failure, it was as if the wind itself was sealed away.
Investigate the damaged western turbine array and determine what happened to the missing current. Location: Main Power Station.
objectives.successDescription: You discover a Dead Current Gauge and evidence that the airflow was abruptly cut off by an artificial force.

objectives.description: Follow the pressure residue through the Turbine Spine Walkway. Location: Turbine Spine Walkway.
objectives.successDescription: Unstable pressure has thrown maintenance drones into chaos.

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw.
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent.
objectives.successDescription: You recover a Pressure Residue Sample while Saeji secures the walkway.

objectives.description: Saeji of the Sky Wardens - Turbine Spine Walkway: This was not sabotage in the usual sense. Something pulled the wind away from these ducts instead of damaging them.
Bring the Pressure Residue Sample to the Chime Calibration Hall for analysis. Location: Chime Calibration Hall.
objectives.successDescription: Elder Shion reveals the missing current has been spiritually silenced rather than destroyed.

objectives.description: Elder Shion - Chime Calibration Hall: The current cannot answer the chime because it has been wrapped in stillness. Take the Silent Chime Core, it will guide you back to the lost wind.
Follow the Silent Chime Core into the Hollow Draft Tunnel. Location: Hollow Draft Tunnel.
objectives.successDescription: The tunnel is unnaturally silent, and the Silent Chime Core begins reacting.

objectives.description: Defeat the Windless Shades formed from dead air pockets.

objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent.

objectives.description: Investigate Fujin's Listening Shrine. Location: Fujin's Listening Shrine.

objectives.description: Elder Shion - Fujin's Listening Shrine: Place the Silent Chime Core near the shrine. The remaining breath of the current will reveal where it has been imprisoned.

nextObjectiveId.text: Use the Pressure Residue Sample with the core.
Force wind chakra into the shrine.

objectives.description: Follow the revealed path into the hidden chamber known as the Windless Eye. Location: The Windless Eye.
objectives.successDescription: A trapped vortex of compressed wind surrounds an ancient pressure seal.

objectives.description: Councilor Iroha - The Windless Eye: That ancient pressure seal has been feeding on the current for years. Whatever is inside is no longer just a seal, it has become something far worse.
Defeat the Stillness Wraith without destroying the trapped wind current.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw.
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent.
objectives.successDescription: You recover the Recovered Wind Core and destroy the ancient pressure seal.

objectives.description: System Narration - The Windless Eye: The current is free but unstable. Guide it safely back to the power station before it overloads the turbines.
Escort the restored current back through the turbine network to the Main Power Station. Location: Main Power Station.
objectives.successDescription: The western turbines begin turning once more as engineers prepare for reintegration.

objectives.description: Toma the Turbine Keeper - Main Power Station: Pressure is stabilizing. The turbines are turning again. The current has finally come home.
Councilor Iroha - Main Power Station: Power has returned across Akikaze. The damage is manageable, but someone or something left an ancient wind trap beneath my mountain. I intend to find out why.
Elder Shion - Main Power Station: The lost wind has returned, but the broken seal is a warning. Old forces still linger beneath Akikaze, waiting to be heard once more.
objectives.successDescription: Quest complete.

objectives.description: System Narration: Your actions destabilize the missing current or delay its recovery. The power station enters emergency shutdown, leaving large sections of Akikaze without power as the Council seals the damaged wind routes.

objectives.description: The Drowned Fleet has come raiding. Its tide-ninja fight inside a churn of water that drinks your blows: when one raises its absorb, hard hits only feed it, while afterburn lands after the absorb step in the exchange and gets clean damage through. data.name: A Call for Aid from the Grovetender
data.description:
A Call for Aid from the Grovetender
Something is wrong in the Shining Expanse. The Sandworms, ancient beasts that sleep beneath the dunes, have begun to rampage. They tear through the land without reason, destroying everything in their path.

I am The Grovetender, guardian of this land. I do not know what has disturbed the Sandworms, but their destruction is spreading. Sunny the Tree, the oldest and most sacred tree in the desert, is in danger. If it falls, the balance of life here will be lost, and the village of Shirohana will suffer.

I cannot stop this alone. I call upon the Global Anbu—warriors of skill and courage—to help defend the tree and uncover the cause of this disaster. Time is running out, and the sands do not wait for anyone.

Will you answer?

—Grovetender of Shirohana
data.successDescription: As the waves crash against the shores of Wake Island, the silence feels almost unreal after the chaos of the desert. The battle with the Alpha Sandworm is over, but its memory lingers—each scar, each grain of sand still clinging to your gear, a reminder of what you faced. The Grovetender’s words echo in your mind, a mix of gratitude and warning, knowing the balance of the dunes has shifted.

objectives.description:
Rain falls from the sky in large droplets as a woman with one black hand and one violet hand watches you, the way a storm watches a field.

"People come for the Reckoning with a list of names," she says.
"Do you want to understand them first? Give me your hands."

Her grip is cold at first but then it's not, the rain you're standing in seems to change and become a different type of rain.
The storm did not break over the ruins of Seichi; it bled into them.

High in the crags, the cult called the "Unbroken Thread" raised two orphaned sisters as a key and not as daughters: "Eclipse", whose chakra pooled black and light-devouring, and Aegis, who heard a dying god in the thunder.

On the eve of their nineteenth winter the Thread bound them to stone and siphoned their blood into old machines; but the sisters broke the ritual, brought the mountain down, and died of poisoned needles in a muddy ditch beside an abandoned road.

A scavenger girl of sixteen knelt in the mud, gave them the last of her water, and covered them with her only blanket.
Eclipse took her right wrist and Aegis took her left.
"Live for us."
"Carry the sky."

After years of travelling along on the roads of Seichi, eventually it leads to a bridge.

Under it a man is bleeding from an execution he escaped, and on the road above the patrols are calling to each other.

"His name is Kaizen Arakuro, and he cannot run."

nextObjectiveId.text: Keep walking. This is not your road.
Pull him into the dark under the bridge and hide him.
Go up and meet the patrol with a blade.

objectives.description:
The memory seizes around your wrists.
That is not what she did.

The memory refuses that shape. Someone once knelt in the mud for her, and whatever she did under that bridge, it was not walk on and it was not draw a blade.
The memory refuses that shape. Someone once knelt in the mud for her, and whatever she did under that bridge, it was not walk on and it was not draw a blade.

The patrol passes.
When the road is quiet Kaizen asks her why, but she doesn't even have to think about it.

Months later; Mira Kagetsu stands in the middle of a scorched field with three hunters dead at her feet and seven more closing in.

data.name: The Path of a Shinobi
data.description:
"The Mortal King," Haki begins, his voice echoing in the stillness, "is no mere legend.
He is a celestial being whose presence alone disturbs the balance of our world.
He walks the line between divinity and mortality, wielding powers that can reshape the very fabric of Seichi."

He gestures toward a map spread across the table.
Marked upon it are several locations where traces of the Mortal King's presence have been detected—places where the laws of nature have been twisted, and chaos has ensued.
Wildfire erupts in the Shining Dunes without cause; eternal storms rage in Akikaze's Whirling Valley; ice forms in Hyorin's Frozen Highlands, not of Kuraokami's making, but of something far more sinister.

"Your mission is to track these disturbances," Haki continues, his eyes locking onto each Chunin in turn.
"Investigate the traces left behind by this celestial figure.
Find out what he seeks, and most importantly, prevent him from reaching the Monarch Powers—ancient forces that, if combined with his celestial abilities, could plunge our world into irreversible darkness."

The Chunin exchange glances, their resolve hardening.
Each of them carries the weight of their village on their shoulders, but none falter.
They understand the stakes—failure is not an option.

Haki pauses, allowing the gravity of his words to sink in.
Then, with a final nod, he concludes, "You will face not just the Mortal King, but those who serve him—beings of great power and deception.
Trust in your training, in each other, and in Seichi.
Dismissed."
data.successDescription:
They have won, but the victory is bittersweet.
Haki, once their leader, now lies defeated and broken.
The Monarch Powers remain beyond their reach, but Seichi is safe—for now.

As they make their way back to the surface, the Chunin know that their journey is far from over.
The world may never know of their sacrifice, of the betrayal they faced, or of the celestial judgment that looms over them.
But they carry the lessons of this mission with them, a reminder that even in the darkest moments, honor and duty must guide their path.

And somewhere, far beyond the mortal realm, the Mortal King watches, waiting for the day when the balance of Seichi will be tested once more. The monarch is coming and this fragile peace will be broken.

Nestled between the Tornado Valley and Windswept Grasslands, the valley is infamous for its brutal winds and treacherous terrain. Yet, this harsh environment has become a refuge for those who serve the celestial figure, hiding in the chaos of the valley's ever-changing landscape.  The Chunin, tasked with tracking down these elusive servants, quickly realize that the Whirling Valley is unlike any other place they have encountered. The wind here is not just a force of nature; it is a barrier, a guardian of secrets. The valley’s relentless gales twist and turn, obscuring paths and covering tracks, making it nearly impossible to follow any conventional trail. The wind howls like a living creature, and the air is thick with the scent of danger.  Every step through the valley is a battle. The ground beneath their feet is unstable, shifting with the constant pressure of the wind. Loose rocks and sharp ridges make the terrain hazardous, and even the most skilled Shinobi must move with caution. But it is not just the physical dangers that test them—there is an eerie presence in the valley, a sense that they are being watched, hunted even, by forces unseen.

objectives.description:
The journey of the Chunin has led them to an ancient ruin in the ironwood forest, a place forgotten by time and untouched by the living. The air is heavy with the presence of the celestial being known as the Mortal King. The ground beneath them hums with energy as they enter the final chamber, a vast space carved from stone and adorned with cryptic symbols that seem to shift and change with every glance. In the center of the chamber, a massive altar looms, pulsing with an otherworldly light. The Chunin can feel the power radiating from it, a force so overwhelming that it threatens to tear apart the fabric of reality itself. They know that this is where the Mortal King plans to unlock the Monarch Powers—a moment that could change the fate of Seichi forever. But as they prepare to confront the celestial being, something feels off. Haki, their enigmatic leader, stands before the altar, his back turned to them. His figure, usually so composed and commanding, now seems shrouded in a dark, almost malevolent energy. One of the Chunin speaks up, their voice laced with concern. "Haki, what are you doing? We need to stop the Mortal King!" Haki doesn't turn to face them. Instead, his voice echoes through the chamber, cold and detached.
"Stop him? No, I have no intention of stopping him. In fact, I have no intention of letting any of you leave this place alive."

objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent
objectives.successDescription: "You... fools,"Haki spits, his voice weak. "You could have had everything. Now you've doomed us all. But before he can say more, the Mortal King finally speaks. His voice is deep and resonant, echoing through the chamber like the tolling of a bell. "Doomed? No. You misunderstand, Haki." The Chunin turn to face the celestial figure, who has remained silent until now. The Mortal King gazes at them with eyes that seem to hold the weight of countless stars. There is no anger in his expression, no malice—only a calm, almost serene acceptance of what has transpired. "I did not intervene because this was never about power," the Mortal King continues. "It was about judgment. You sought to claim what was not yours, Haki, and in doing so, you revealed the darkness within your heart. But these Chunin—despite their trials, despite your betrayal—chose to act with honor. The Mortal King raises a hand, and for a moment, it seems as though he might unleash his celestial power upon them all. But instead, he simply turns away, his form beginning to dissolve into light. "The balance of Seichi will be restored," he says, his voice fading. "But remember this, mortals: true power lies not in strength or ambition, but in understanding the limits of one's own desires. I will be watching."

data.name: [Path of Crimson] [Part II: The Ember Trail]
data.description:
The sky glows with the colors of twilight as Dusk stands at the edge of Wake Island, his golden scarf flickering in the breeze. His gaze is distant, his expression thoughtful, but when you approach, he turns to you with a faint smirk.

"Ah, there you are. I thought perhaps the embers had swallowed you, but you’re too stubborn for that, aren’t you?"

His smirk fades, and he gestures toward a map spread across a nearby stone. The parchment is old, singed at the edges, with three locations marked: The Flamebinding Altar, Infernal Pool, and Ember Crossroads.

"The Black Maw’s flames burn hotter along the Ember Trail. This isn’t just another raid—they’re targeting sacred sites. These seals aren’t just relics. They’re bindings, meant to hold dangerous energies. If they succeed in breaking them, the fires won’t stop with these sites."

He looks back at you, his tone quieter but heavier with meaning.

"Seals like these don’t just break—they shatter. Shadows twist, fire spreads, and what’s unleashed doesn’t go back easily. You’ll need to stop them. Follow the trail, disrupt their rituals, and bring me anything you find."

He pauses, his fiery scarf shifting slightly, as though caught in an unseen current.

"And be careful. What the Maw touches leaves marks that don’t fade."

As he hands you the map, his eyes meet yours, the intensity behind them unmistakable.

"Go. Fire destroys, but it also reveals. Just don’t let it consume you."

His gaze lingers on the horizon for a moment before he turns back to the village, his scarf glowing faintly in the dimming light.

You stumble across something you... might have wish you hadn't. They saw you.
You're in it now, kid.

data.name: Shadows in the Updraft: The Lost Current
data.description: A Genin side story in Akikaze Village. A routine wind-gauge inspection uncovers the Lost Current, a missing Sky Maiden, and treason inside the Sky Wardens.
data.successDescription: You survive Kael's vacuum burst and carry Yumi's evidence out of the tunnels. The Divine Fragment is gone, but the conspiracy is exposed.

objectives.description: The copper vanes of the Lower Spires whir with their usual drone, but your brass anemometer shows the primary updraft from the Third Vent dropping fast.
Senior Warden Kael drops from a guide-rail above you. He jokes at first, then sees the readings and goes still.
You warn that a thirty percent drop could destabilize the commercial platforms below the Spire of Whispers by dusk.
Kael calls it the Lost Current and tells you to file the report with Civil Harmony. His tone makes the order feel like a wall.
Bypass Civil Harmony and climb toward the Spire of Whispers to look for someone willing to speak plainly.
Near the launch platforms, Yumi struggles to reel in a massive oracle kite. Its chakra-conductive script is scorched and torn to ribbons.
You identify the damage as vacuum-blade scoring, not heat. Yumi realizes you are paying attention to the right details.
Yumi says someone is rerouting the core wind channels with high-altitude Aero-Vault technology.
The Sky Maiden investigated the auxiliary vents last night and never returned. Yumi says the silence around her disappearance is deliberate.
Yumi names the Rogue Wardens, a splinter faction inside Kael's division, as the ones who caused the power drop.
Tomorrow's Zephyr Kage ascension will happen with Akikaze's barrier network weakened. An assassin could cross the sky-bridges unseen.
Navigate the Dust Maelstrom tunnels beneath the village, following fine sand patterns disturbed by unnatural vacuum pressure.
The trail leads to a hidden auxiliary terminal tied directly to the main power station.
Kael stands before a pressurized Aero-Vault, extracting an incandescent blue Divine Fragment used to stabilize the regional atmosphere.
Kael says the Council worships flow while Akikaze stagnates. He claims the new Zephyr Kage will disarm the village into weakness.
Kael admits the Sky Maiden is bound in the upper sanctuary. He insists she will be released once the transition of power fails.
Yumi bursts from an overhead ventilation duct and disrupts Kael's vacuum field with chakra-infused oracle daggers.
Yumi exposes the deeper betrayal: Kael is selling Akikaze's defensive layout to an underground faction from Shroud.
Kael says you are both too late. The currents have already shifted. He unleashes a localized vacuum that steals the air from your lungs.
You survive long enough to carry Yumi's evidence out of the tunnels. Kael has escaped with the Divine Fragment, but the Lost Current conspiracy is no longer hidden.

data.name: The Silent Bells of Winter
data.description: A supernatural winter has descended without wind or warning. Snowmen appear where none were built, and silent Moonprowlers circle the settlements. At the center of this anomaly is a massive, sentient snowman—Ava the Snow Terror. She is invulnerable to standard steel. You must hunt her elven lieutenants, Axel and Dagger, and the prowling beasts to gather the materials needed to forge the Candy Cane Blade, the only weapon capable of cracking her frost-core.
data.successDescription: The Candy Cane Blade strikes true, shattering Ava's frost-core. The unnatural winter breaks instantly. The snowmen collapse into harmless drifts, the elves vanish, and the haunting bells finally fall silent. The village is safe, though the memory of the watching snow will linger forever.

objectives.description: The snow fell without warning. No storm. No wind. Just... silence. And now She is here. Ava, the Snow Terror. She stands taller than the roofs, watching. We cannot hurt her; she rebuilds herself instantly. But the legends speak of a weapon—the Candy Cane Blade. Only it can crack her core. You must gather the parts and forge it yourself. Seek the beasts at the treeline first
Head to the Moonlit Treeline where the Moonprowlers are circling the village.

data.name: The Concord Table
data.description: Forty years of war end tonight at one table in Kilnreach, and every house seated there has already paid for your services. Three doors in. Five favors out. The door you take decides everything after it.
data.successDescription: One favor stood, one signet earned, and the Concord survives its first night. The table seats five houses and one empty chair, and somewhere in Kilnreach a dead fire is warm.

objectives.description: The letter finds you at dusk, unsigned, unhurried. One seal in five colors, pressed once. Forty years of war end tonight at a table in Kilnreach, and every house seated there has already paid for your services. The Concord Table convenes at moonrise. Come as you are, or as someone useful.

Kilnreach's Concord hall has three ways in, and the way you enter is the person you are all night. The front gate takes guests. The service terraces take staff. The kiln tunnels below take no names at all.

nextObjectiveId.text: The front gate, as a guest

objectives.description: The front gate swallows you into lamplight and perfume. Guests are courted here, watched here, and priced here, usually in that order.
Three conversations glitter within reach of the wine. Which do you drift toward?

nextObjectiveId.text: The widow with the red thread

objectives.description: Two Brassmark cousins argue over whether peace is cheaper than war. They conclude, with some sorrow, that it is.
An old woman winds red thread through her fingers and watches everyone who watches her. She smiles at you a beat too early.
Orchard people speak softly about harvests and softer about funerals. Nobody in the circle drinks first.
A wall of ceremony steps into your path: the Kilnreach Doorwarden, who decides who is a guest and who is merely inside. Your invitation, it seems, requires a demonstration.
The Doorwarden rolls one shoulder. The demonstration begins.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You are helped politely off the floor. The gate does not apologize; it simply waits for a better demonstration.
The Doorwarden bows a fraction of an inch, which in this hall is a standing ovation. Doors that were pretending to be walls quietly resume being doors.
You pass the Concord Table itself on the way in: five chairs, five draperies, one chair unclaimed and older than the rest. Nobody looks at the empty one, which is how you know everybody is.
With standing comes access. Three quiet sources offer an evening's intelligence.
The chart shows who sits beside whom, and more usefully, who refused to. The Ironbrood and the Brassmark share a border and nothing else.
The steward has poured for four decades of truces. He rates this one 'a strong vintage, drunk too young'.
The old chair's arms are worn smooth in the grip pattern of one pair of hands. Whoever sat here, sat here for years, and left nothing else behind.
Midnight. Favors come due, and a guest may carry only one. Three houses have made their interest in you explicit.
The service terraces take you in through steam and shouted orders. Staff go everywhere, see everything, and are seen by no one who matters.
Three knots of workers trade the evening's real news. Where do you lend a hand and an ear?
The dishwashers know which house sent back its food untouched. The Orchard's plates come back full and their people leave healthy.
The porters carried a chest up from the tunnels that clinked like coin and was signed for like a body.
The lamplighters were paid to leave two corridors dark tonight. They will not say which, but they took the money twice.
The Terrace Foreman blocks the stair with a clipboard and a lifetime of saying no. Unfamiliar staff get one interview, conducted with fists.
The Foreman sets down the clipboard carefully. The interview begins.
objectives.drawDescription: The battle ended in a draw
objectives.failDescription: You failed to defeat the opponent

objectives.description: You wake stacked with the crates. The Foreman's clipboard has a fresh note beside your name: 'again'.
The Foreman hauls you up and signs you off as 'adequate', the highest grade the terraces award. The house is yours to move through now.
A serving route takes you along the Concord Table's blind side. Up close the five draperies are patched and re-dyed; the peace has been rehearsed before. The sixth chair has no drapery at all.
Staff hear what guests never will. Three doors are ajar tonight.
The Charnel Guild has requisitioned lamp oil, lime, and silence for the under-halls. Salvage work, on a night like this.
The ledger shows the Ironbrood's pit stores doubled this week. Someone expects the challenge circle to be busy.
Voices carry up the shaft: two houses rehearsing tomorrow's argument tonight, word for word, like a script.
The night shift turns over, and with it the favors. Staff may carry one. Three houses have left word for you below stairs.
The kiln tunnels ask no names and give no light you don't bring. Down here the Concord is just weather happening to other people.
Three fires burn low in the under-dark, each with its own congregation. Whose warmth do you share?
Runners trade routes and prices. Every route tonight ends at the hall above, and every price has tripled.
Charnel diggers rest on their spades. They dig where they're paid to and remember everything they cover up.
The oldest fire keeps the oldest story: about the founder of the peace, who came down here once, and what she planted.
A chain rattles taut across the tunnel: the Toll-Cutter, who taxes everything that moves in the dark. Tonight the toll is proof you can refuse to pay it.
The Toll-Cutter grins around a missing tooth. The toll comes due.
